title.zh: 卷一百九十七 列傳第一百二十二 循吏
title.raw: 卷一百九十七 列傳第一百二十二 循吏 Volume 197 Biographies 122: Virtuous Officials

sentences.zh: 治者，君也；

translations.literal: The one who governs is the ruler;
translations.idiomatic: The ruler is the one who governs;

sentences.zh: 求所以治者，民也；

translations.literal: those who seek the means of governance are the people;
translations.idiomatic: the people are those who seek good governance;

sentences.zh: 推君之治而濟之民，吏也。

translations.literal: those who extend the ruler's governance and bring benefit to the people are the officials.
translations.idiomatic: Officials are the ones who carry out the ruler's policies and bring relief to the people.

sentences.zh: 故吏良則法平政成，不良則王道馳而敗矣。

translations.literal: Therefore when officials are good, the law is fair and government succeeds; when they are not good, the royal way slackens and fails.
translations.idiomatic: When officials are capable, the law is even-handed and governance succeeds; when they are not, the kingly way falters and collapses.

sentences.zh: 在堯、舜時，曰「九德咸事」也，「百工惟時」也；

translations.literal: In the time of Yao and Shun, it was said, 'The nine virtues all have their tasks,' and 'The hundred offices each keep their season';
translations.idiomatic: Under Yao and Shun it was said that 'all nine virtues had their proper work' and that 'every office kept its proper season';

sentences.zh: 在周文、武時，曰「《棫樸》，能官人也」，「《南山有臺》，樂得賢也」；

translations.literal: In the time of King Wen and King Wu of Zhou, it was said, 'The Ode of Yue Pu shows the ability to appoint men to office,' and 'The Ode of South Mountain Terrace rejoices in obtaining the worthy';
translations.idiomatic: Under Kings Wen and Wu of Zhou it was said that the 'Ode of Yue Pu' praised the ability to appoint men to office, and the 'Ode of South Mountain Terrace' celebrated the joy of finding worthy men;

sentences.zh: 是循吏之效也。

translations.literal: this is the effect of virtuous officials.
translations.idiomatic: such is the achievement of virtuous officials.

sentences.zh: 堯、舜，五帝之盛帝，文、武，三王之顯王，不能去是而治，後世可乎哉？

translations.literal: Yao and Shun were the greatest emperors among the Five Emperors; Wen and Wu were the most illustrious kings among the Three Kings — they could not govern by abandoning this principle; how could later ages do so?
translations.idiomatic: Yao and Shun were the greatest of the Five Emperors, and Wen and Wu the most illustrious of the Three Kings — neither could govern without this principle. How then could later ages hope to do so?

sentences.zh: 唐興，承隋亂離，祓荒荼，始擇用州刺史、縣令。

translations.literal: When Tang arose, inheriting the chaos and separation of Sui, clearing away desolation and suffering, it began to select and employ prefects and magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tang dynasty rose, inheriting the chaos and ruin left by Sui, it began clearing away desolation and carefully choosing prefects and county magistrates.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗曰：「朕思天下事，丙夜不安枕，永惟治人之本，莫重刺史，故錄姓名於屏風，臥興對之，得才否狀，輒疏之下方，以擬廢置。」

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong once said: 'When I think of affairs under Heaven, I cannot rest my head on the pillow even in the third watch of the night. Ever considering the root of governing the people, nothing is more important than prefects. Therefore I record their names on a screen; when I rise or lie down I face it. When I learn whether they have talent or not, I immediately write notes below, intending appointment or dismissal.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong once said: 'When I ponder affairs under Heaven, I cannot sleep even past midnight. I have always held that nothing matters more for governing the people than prefects. So I write their names on a screen and face it whenever I rise or lie down. As soon as I learn whether each man has ability, I jot notes beneath his name to decide whether to keep or remove him.'

sentences.zh: 又詔內外官五品以上舉任縣令者。

translations.literal: He also issued an edict that officials inside and outside the court of fifth rank and above should recommend candidates for county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered that all officials inside and outside the court of fifth rank and above recommend candidates for county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 於是官得其人，民去嘆愁、就妥安。

translations.literal: Thereupon offices obtained the right men, and the people left sighs of sorrow and attained peace and security.
translations.idiomatic: Offices were thus filled with the right men, and the people left behind their sighs of hardship and found peace.

sentences.zh: 都督、刺史，其職察州縣，間遣使者循行天下，劾舉不職。

translations.literal: The duties of regional commanders and prefects were to inspect prefectures and counties; from time to time envoys were sent to tour the realm and impeach those who failed in their duties.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commanders and prefects were charged with overseeing prefectures and counties, and from time to time envoys were sent throughout the realm to impeach officials who neglected their duties.

sentences.zh: 始，都督、刺史皆天子臨軒冊授。

translations.literal: At first, regional commanders and prefects were all invested by the Son of Heaven in person at the imperial hall.
translations.idiomatic: At first, regional commanders and prefects were all personally invested by the emperor in the imperial hall.

sentences.zh: 後不復冊，然猶受命日對便殿，賜衣物，乃遣。

translations.literal: Later they were no longer invested by edict, but on the day they received their commission they still appeared before the side hall, were granted clothing, and then were dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: Later the formal investiture ceased, but on the day they received their commissions they still appeared before the side hall, received gifts of clothing, and only then were sent off.

sentences.zh: 玄宗開元時，已辭，仍詣側門候進止，所以光寵守臣，以責其功。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era of Emperor Xuanzong, even after taking leave of audience, they still went to the side gate to await further orders — thus to honor frontier officials and hold them accountable for their achievements.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Xuanzong's Kaiyuan era, even after being dismissed from audience, appointees still waited at the side gate for further instructions — a mark of honor for frontier officials and a way to hold them accountable for their work.

sentences.zh: 初，刺史準京官得佩魚，品卑者假緋、魚。

translations.literal: At first, prefects, following capital officials, were permitted to wear the fish tally; those of lower rank were lent scarlet robes and fish tallies.
translations.idiomatic: At first prefects, like capital officials, were allowed to wear the fish tally; those of lower rank were lent scarlet robes and fish insignia.

sentences.zh: 開元中，又錮廢酷吏，懲無良，群臣化之，革苛嬈之風，爭以惠利顯。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan period, harsh officials were again shackled and removed, and the wicked were punished. The ministers were transformed by this, reformed the harsh and oppressive customs, and competed to display benevolence and benefit.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaiyuan, harsh officials were again removed from office and the corrupt were punished. The court followed suit, abandoning oppressive practices and competing to show themselves as bringers of benefit to the people.

sentences.zh: 復詔：三省侍郎缺，擇嘗任刺史者；

translations.literal: An edict was again issued: when vice-minister posts in the Three Departments were vacant, those who had once served as prefects were to be chosen;
translations.idiomatic: Another edict declared that when vice-minister posts in the Three Departments fell vacant, preference should go to men who had served as prefects;

sentences.zh: 郎官缺，擇嘗任縣令者。

translations.literal: when courtier posts were vacant, those who had once served as county magistrates were to be chosen.
translations.idiomatic: and when courtier posts fell vacant, men who had served as county magistrates were to be chosen.

sentences.zh: 至宰相名臣，莫不孜孜言長人不可輕授亟易。

translations.literal: Down to chief ministers and renowned ministers, none failed to speak earnestly that the task of governing the people must not be lightly entrusted or frequently changed.
translations.idiomatic: Even chief ministers and celebrated statesmen all insisted that governing the people must not be entrusted lightly or changed too often.

sentences.zh: 是以授受之間，雖不能皆善，而所得十五。

translations.literal: Therefore, in the matter of appointment and transfer, although not all could be good, about seven or eight out of ten were successful.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, although not every appointment was ideal, roughly seven or eight out of ten proved successful.

sentences.zh: 故葉氣嘉生，薰為太平，垂祀三百，與漢相埒。

translations.literal: Therefore auspicious qi flourished, perfuming the age into great peace; the dynasty endured for three hundred years, rivaling Han.
translations.idiomatic: Auspicious influences flourished and the age ripened into great peace; the dynasty endured for three hundred years, rivaling the Han.

sentences.zh: 致之之術，非循吏謂何？

translations.literal: The means of achieving this — if not virtuous officials, then what?
translations.idiomatic: If this achievement was not owed to virtuous officials, then to what was it owed?

sentences.zh: 故條次治宜，以著厥庸。

translations.literal: Therefore their governing achievements are arranged in order to record their merits.
translations.idiomatic: Their governing achievements are therefore set forth in order to record their merits.

sentences.zh: 若將相大臣兼以勛閥著者，名見本篇，不列於茲。

translations.literal: As for ministers and generals who are also noted for meritorious clans, their names appear in this chapter but are not listed here.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers and generals who are also noted for distinguished lineage appear elsewhere in this chapter and are not listed here.

sentences.zh: 韋仁壽，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Wei Renshou was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Renshou was from Wannian in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 隋大業末，為蜀郡司法書佐，斷獄平，得罪者皆自以韋君所論，死無恨。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye era of Sui, he served as judicial clerk of Shu Commandery. His judgments in cases were fair, and those punished all considered Wei Jun's rulings just; even those condemned to death had no resentment.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Sui's Daye era he served as judicial clerk of Shu Commandery. His verdicts were fair, and even those condemned to death accepted Wei Jun's judgments without resentment.

sentences.zh: 高祖入關，遣使者徇定蜀，承制擢仁壽巂州都督府長史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu entered the Pass, he sent envoys to pacify and settle Shu, and by provisional order promoted Renshou to chief secretary of the Yizhou Regional Command.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu entered the Pass, he sent envoys to pacify Shu and provisionally promoted Renshou to chief secretary of the Yizhou Regional Command.

sentences.zh: 南寧州納款，朝廷歲遣使撫接，至率貪沓，邊人苦之，多叛去。

translations.literal: Nanning Prefecture submitted allegiance, and the court each year sent envoys to soothe and receive them, but these envoys were generally greedy and grasping; the frontier people suffered from this and many rebelled and left.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanning Prefecture submitted, the court sent annual envoys to win over the region, but they were habitually greedy and corrupt; the frontier people suffered and many rebelled.

sentences.zh: 帝素聞仁壽治理，詔檢校南寧州都督，寄治越巂，詔歲一按行尉勞。

translations.literal: The emperor had long heard of Renshou's governance and ordered him to serve as acting military commissioner of Nanning Prefecture, with his seat at Yuexi, and decreed that once a year he should tour and comfort the region.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, having long heard of Renshou's ability, appointed him acting military commissioner of Nanning Prefecture with his seat at Yuexi, and ordered him to tour and comfort the region once a year.

sentences.zh: 仁壽將兵五百人，循西洱河，開地數千里，稱詔置七州十五縣，酋豪皆來賓見，即授以牧宰，威令簡嚴，人人安悅。

translations.literal: Renshou led five hundred soldiers, followed the West Er River, and opened territory for several thousand li; by proclaimed edict he established seven prefectures and fifteen counties. Tribal chiefs all came to pay homage, and he immediately appointed them as local governors. His authority was simple and strict, and everyone was secure and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Renshou led five hundred soldiers along the West Er River and opened territory stretching thousands of li. By proclaimed edict he established seven prefectures and fifteen counties. Tribal chiefs came to pay homage and he immediately appointed them as local governors. His rule was simple yet firm, and the people were secure and content.

sentences.zh: 將還，酋長泣曰：「天子藉公鎮撫，奈何欲去我？」

translations.literal: When he was about to return, the chieftains wept and said: 'The Son of Heaven relies on you, sir, to pacify and soothe us — how can you wish to leave us?'
translations.idiomatic: When he prepared to leave, the chieftains wept and said: 'The Son of Heaven relies on you to govern us — how can you abandon us?'

sentences.zh: 仁壽以池壁未立為解，諸酋即相率築城起廨，甫旬略具。

translations.literal: Renshou explained that the walls and fortifications had not yet been built. The chiefs at once jointly built walls and erected offices, and in barely ten days the essentials were complete.
translations.idiomatic: Renshou replied that the walls and fortifications were not yet built. The chiefs immediately joined together to build walls and erect offices, and in barely ten days the essentials were complete.

sentences.zh: 仁壽乃告以實曰：「吾奉詔第撫循，庸敢擅留？」

translations.literal: Renshou then told them the truth, saying: 'I received an edict merely to pacify and tour — how would I dare to stay on my own authority?'
translations.idiomatic: Renshou then told them plainly: 'I was sent only to pacify and inspect — how could I dare stay on my own authority?'

sentences.zh: 夷夏父老乃悲啼祖行，遣子弟隨貢方物，天子大悅。

translations.literal: The elders of both barbarian and Chinese wept and saw him off on his journey; they sent their sons and younger brothers to accompany tribute goods. The Son of Heaven was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian and Chinese elders wept as they saw him off, sending their sons to accompany tribute goods to court. The emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 仁壽請徙治南寧州，假兵遂撫定，詔可，敕益州給兵護送。

translations.literal: Renshou requested to move his seat of government to Nanning Prefecture, borrow troops, and then pacify and settle the region. The edict approved, and Yizhou was ordered to supply soldiers to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: Renshou asked to move his seat to Nanning Prefecture, borrow troops, and complete the pacification. The request was approved and Yizhou was ordered to supply soldiers as escort.

sentences.zh: 刺史竇軌疾其功，訹言山獠方叛，未可以遠略，不時遣。

translations.literal: The prefect Dou Gui envied his achievement and slandered him, saying the mountain Liao were just then rebelling and a distant campaign was not yet possible; the troops were not sent in time.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Dou Gui, jealous of his achievement, slandered him, claiming the mountain tribes were rebelling and a distant campaign was impossible; the troops were never sent.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，卒。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he died.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later, he died.

sentences.zh: 陳君賓，陳鄱陽王伯山子也。

translations.literal: Chen Junbin was the son of Chen Prince of Poyang, Bo Shan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Junbin was the son of Bo Shan, Prince of Poyang of Chen.

sentences.zh: 仕隋為襄國通守。

translations.literal: He served Sui as defender-general of Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: He served the Sui as defender-general of Xiangguo.

sentences.zh: 武德初，挈郡聽命，封東陽郡公，遷邢州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude, he brought his commandery to submit, was enfeoffed as Duke of Dongyang Commandery, and was transferred to prefect of Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Wude he submitted his commandery, was enfeoffed as Duke of Dongyang Commandery, and was appointed prefect of Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，徙鄧州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, he was transferred to Deng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Zhenguan he was transferred to Deng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 州承喪亂後，百姓流冗，君賓加意勞徠，不期月，皆還自業。

translations.literal: The prefecture, having suffered the aftermath of war and chaos, had a populace scattered and displaced. Junbin paid special attention to encouraging and welcoming them, and within less than a month all returned to their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture had been devastated by war and the people were scattered. Junbin worked hard to encourage them to return, and within a month they had all resumed their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 明年，四方霜潦，獨君賓所治有年，儲倉充羨，蒲、虞二州民就食其境。

translations.literal: The next year, frost and floods struck everywhere, but only in Junbin's jurisdiction was there a good harvest; the storehouses were full to overflowing, and the people of Pu and Yu prefectures came to his territory for food.
translations.idiomatic: The next year frost and floods struck everywhere, but only Junbin's jurisdiction had a good harvest. Storehouses overflowed, and people from Pu and Yu prefectures came to his region for food.

sentences.zh: 太宗下詔勞之曰：「去年關內六州谷不登，糇糧少，令析民房逐食。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong issued an edict commending him, saying: 'Last year in six prefectures within the Pass the grain did not ripen; provisions were scarce, and I ordered the people to disperse to find food.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong issued an edict praising him: 'Last year six prefectures within the Pass failed to harvest; provisions were scarce and I ordered the people to disperse in search of food.

sentences.zh: 聞刺史與百姓識朕此懷，務相安養，還有贏糧，出布帛贈遺行者。

translations.literal: I hear that the prefect and the people understood my intent, strove to settle and nourish one another, and even had surplus grain, giving out cloth and silk as gifts to those who traveled on.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that you and your people understood my intent, cared for one another in peace, and even had surplus grain, giving cloth and silk to travelers.

sentences.zh: 此知水旱常數，更相拯贍，禮讓興行，海內之人皆為兄弟，變澆薄之風，朕顧何憂？

translations.literal: This shows that you know floods and droughts are a regular occurrence, that people aid and support one another, that courtesy and yielding flourish, that all within the seas are as brothers, and that the shallow and harsh customs are transformed — what have I to worry about?
translations.idiomatic: This shows you understand that flood and drought are part of nature, that people aid one another, that courtesy flourishes, that all under Heaven are as brothers, and that harsh customs are being transformed — what have I to worry about?

sentences.zh: 已命有司錄刺史以下功最；

translations.literal: I have already ordered the relevant offices to record the outstanding achievements of the prefect and those below him;
translations.idiomatic: I have ordered the relevant offices to record the achievements of the prefect and his subordinates;

sentences.zh: 百姓養戶，免今年調物。」

translations.literal: households that hosted the people are exempt from this year's tax levies.'
translations.idiomatic: and households that hosted refugees are exempt from this year's tax levies.'

sentences.zh: 是歲，入為太府少卿，轉少府少監，坐事免。

translations.literal: That year he entered the capital as vice director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, was transferred to vice director of the Palace Workshops, and was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: That year he entered the capital as vice director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, was transferred to vice director of the Palace Workshops, and was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 起為虔州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: He was recalled to serve as prefect of Qian Prefecture and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as prefect of Qian Prefecture and died in office.

sentences.zh: 張允濟，青州北海人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yunji was a native of Beihai in Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yunji was from Beihai in Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 仕隋為武陽令，以愛利為行。

translations.literal: He served Sui as magistrate of Wuyang, taking benevolence and benefit as his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He served the Sui as magistrate of Wuyang, conducting himself with benevolence and public benefit.

sentences.zh: 元武民以牸牛依婦家者，久之，孳十餘犢，將歸，而婦家不與牛。

translations.literal: A man of Yuanwu had left a cow with his wife's family; after a long time it bore more than ten calves. When he was about to take them back, his wife's family would not give him the cattle.
translations.idiomatic: A man of Yuanwu had left a cow with his wife's family; over time it bore more than ten calves. When he came to take them back, his in-laws refused to return the cattle.

sentences.zh: 民訴縣，縣不能決，乃詣允濟，允濟曰：「若自有令，吾何與為？」

translations.literal: The man appealed to the county, but the county could not decide the case, so he went to Yunji. Yunji said: 'If you have your own magistrate, what business is it of mine?'
translations.idiomatic: The man appealed to the county, which could not decide the case, so he went to Yunji. Yunji said: 'You have your own magistrate — what business is this of mine?'

sentences.zh: 民泣訴其抑，允濟因令左右縛民，蒙其首，過婦家，雲捕盜牛者，命盡出民家牛，質所來，婦家不知，遽曰：「此婿家牛，我無豫。」

translations.literal: The man wept and complained of oppression. Yunji then ordered his attendants to bind the man and cover his head, pass by the wife's family, and say they were arresting a cattle thief; he ordered all the cattle from the man's household to be brought out and identified by origin. The wife's family, not knowing the ruse, immediately said: 'These are the son-in-law's cattle; I have nothing to do with them.'
translations.idiomatic: The man wept that he was being wronged. Yunji had his attendants bind the man and cover his head, then pass by the in-laws' home claiming to arrest a cattle thief. He ordered all cattle from the man's household brought out for identification. The in-laws, unaware of the ruse, immediately said: 'These are the son-in-law's cattle — they have nothing to do with us.'

sentences.zh: 即遣左右撤蒙，曰：「可以此牛還婿家。」

translations.literal: He immediately ordered his attendants to remove the covering and said: 'These cattle may be returned to the son-in-law's family.'
translations.idiomatic: He immediately had the covering removed and said: 'These cattle may be returned to the son-in-law's family.'

sentences.zh: 婦家叩頭服罪，元武吏大慚。

translations.literal: The wife's family kowtowed and admitted guilt; the officials of Yuanwu were deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: The in-laws kowtowed in admission of guilt, and the officials of Yuanwu were deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 允濟過道旁，有姥廬守所蒔蔥，因教曰：「第還舍，脫有盜，當告令。」

translations.literal: Yunji passed by the roadside where an old woman had a hut guarding scallions she had planted, and instructed her: 'Just return home; if there is theft, report it to the magistrate.'
translations.idiomatic: Passing a roadside hut where an old woman guarded scallions she had planted, Yunji told her: 'Go home; if anything is stolen, report it to the magistrate.'

sentences.zh: 姥謝歸。

translations.literal: The old woman thanked him and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: The old woman thanked him and went home.

sentences.zh: 俄大亡蔥，允濟召十里內男女盡至，物色驗之，果得盜者。

translations.literal: Soon a large quantity of scallions was stolen. Yunji summoned all men and women within ten li, identified and examined them, and indeed found the thief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a large quantity of scallions was stolen. Yunji summoned all men and women within ten li, examined them, and found the thief.

sentences.zh: 有行人夜發，遺袍道中，行十餘里乃寤，人曰：「吾境未嘗拾遺，可還取之。」

translations.literal: A traveler set out at night and left his robe on the road; after traveling more than ten li he awoke to the loss. Someone said: 'In our territory we never keep lost property — you may go back and retrieve it.'
translations.idiomatic: A traveler set out at night and left his robe on the road; after more than ten li he realized his loss. Someone told him: 'Lost property is never kept in our territory — you may go back and retrieve it.'

sentences.zh: 既而得袍。

translations.literal: He did so and recovered the robe.
translations.idiomatic: He did so and recovered the robe.

sentences.zh: 舉政尤異，遷高陽郡丞，郡缺太守，獨統郡事，吏下畏悅。

translations.literal: His governance was especially outstanding; he was promoted to assistant administrator of Gaoyang Commandery. When the commandery lacked a grand administrator, he alone directed its affairs; officials and subordinates both feared and delighted in him.
translations.idiomatic: His governance was especially outstanding. He was promoted to assistant administrator of Gaoyang Commandery and, when the commandery lacked a grand administrator, directed its affairs alone. Officials both feared and admired him.

sentences.zh: 賊帥王須拔攻郡，於是糧屈，吏食槐葉槁節，無叛者。

translations.literal: When the bandit chief Wang Xuba attacked the commandery, provisions ran short; officials ate locust leaves and withered stalks, yet none rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandit chief Wang Xuba attacked the commandery, provisions ran out and officials ate locust leaves and withered stalks, yet none deserted.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，累遷刑部侍郎，封武城縣男，擢幽州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, he was repeatedly promoted to vice minister of justice, enfeoffed as Baron of Wucheng County, and elevated to prefect of You Prefecture; he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Zhenguan he rose to vice minister of justice, was enfeoffed as Baron of Wucheng County, was appointed prefect of You Prefecture, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 時又有李桐客者，亦以治稱。

translations.literal: At this time there was also Li Tongke, who was likewise famed for his governance.
translations.idiomatic: At this time there was also Li Tongke, likewise renowned for his governance.

sentences.zh: 初仕隋，為門下錄事。

translations.literal: He first served Sui as a clerk in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He first served the Sui as a clerk in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 煬帝在江都，以四方日亂，謀徙都丹楊，召群臣議。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang was at Jiangdu, seeing the realm growing daily more chaotic, he planned to move the capital to Danyang and summoned the ministers to discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang was at Jiangdu and saw the realm growing more chaotic each day, he planned to move the capital to Danyang and summoned his ministers to discuss it.

sentences.zh: 左右希意，以為江左且望幸，若巡狩勒石紀功，復禹舊跡，顧不其然。

translations.literal: Those around him sought to please him, thinking that the lands south of the Yangzi were already awaiting the imperial visit, and that if he toured, inscribed stone to record achievements, and restored the old traces of Yu — would it not be so?
translations.idiomatic: Those around him sought to please him, arguing that the lands south of the Yangzi already awaited the imperial visit, and that a tour to inscribe stone monuments and restore Yu's old traces would be fitting.

sentences.zh: 桐客獨曰：「吳會卑濕而狹，不足奉萬乘、給三軍，吳人力屈，無以堪命，且逾越險阻，非社稷福。

translations.literal: Tongke alone said: 'Wu and Kuai are low, damp, and narrow — insufficient to support the imperial carriage or supply the three armies. The people of Wu are exhausted and cannot bear the burden; moreover, crossing dangerous and obstructed terrain is no blessing to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Tongke alone objected: 'Wu and Kuai are low, damp, and narrow — insufficient to support the imperial carriage or supply the armies. The people of Wu are exhausted and cannot bear the burden; moreover, crossing dangerous terrain would bring no blessing to the state.

sentences.zh: 御史劾以訕毀，幾得罪而免。

translations.literal: The censor impeached him for slander and defamation; he nearly suffered punishment but was spared.
translations.idiomatic: A censor impeached him for slander; he nearly suffered punishment but was spared.

sentences.zh: 為宇文化及脅，將至黎陽，又陷竇建德。

translations.literal: He was coerced by Yuwen Huaji and taken as far as Liyang, then fell into the hands of Dou Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: He was coerced by Yuwen Huaji and taken as far as Liyang, then fell captive to Dou Jiande.

sentences.zh: 賊平，授秦王府法曹參軍。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, he was appointed legal officer of the Prince of Qin's household.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were pacified, he was appointed legal officer in the Prince of Qin's household.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，累為通、巴二州刺史，治尚清平，民呼為慈父。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, he served successively as prefect of Tong and Ba prefectures; his governance valued clarity and fairness, and the people called him the Merciful Father.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Zhenguan he served successively as prefect of Tong and Ba prefectures. His governance was clear and fair, and the people called him the Merciful Father.

sentences.zh: 桐客，冀州衡水人。

translations.literal: Tongke was a native of Hengshui in Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Tongke was from Hengshui in Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 李素立，趙州高邑人。

translations.literal: Li Suli was a native of Gaoyi in Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Suli was from Gaoyi in Zhao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 曾祖義深，仕北齊為梁州刺史。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yishen served Northern Qi as prefect of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yishen served Northern Qi as prefect of Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 父政藻，為隋水部郎，使淮南，死於盜。

translations.literal: His father Zhengzao served Sui as a director in the Ministry of Waterways; on a mission to Huainan he was killed by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhengzao served the Sui as a director in the Ministry of Waterways; on a mission to Huainan he was killed by bandits.

sentences.zh: 素立仕武德初，擢監察御史。

translations.literal: Suli entered service at the beginning of Wude and was promoted to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Suli entered service at the start of Wude and was promoted to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 民犯法不及死，高祖欲殺之，素立諫曰：「三尺法，天下所共有，一動搖，則人無以措手足。

translations.literal: A commoner violated the law but the offense did not warrant death; Emperor Gaozu wished to execute him. Suli remonstrated, saying: 'The law measured by the three-foot rod is shared by all under Heaven; once it is shaken, people have nowhere to place their hands and feet.
translations.idiomatic: A commoner broke the law but the offense did not warrant death; Emperor Gaozu wished to execute him. Suli remonstrated: 'The law is shared by all under Heaven; once it is shaken, people have nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 方大業經始，奈何輦轂下先棄刑書傘？」

translations.literal: Just as great enterprise is beginning, how can we beneath the imperial carriage first abandon the umbrella of the penal code?'
translations.idiomatic: Just as great enterprise is beginning, how can we at the capital first cast aside the shield of the penal code?'

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納，由是恩顧特異。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted this, and from then on showed him special favor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and accepted this, and from then on showed him special favor.

sentences.zh: 以親喪解官，起授七品清要，有司擬雍州司戶參軍，帝曰：「要而不清。」

translations.literal: He resigned on account of mourning for a parent, then was recalled and granted a seventh-rank post that was both important and prestigious. The relevant offices proposed him as registrar of Yong Prefecture. The emperor said: 'Important but not prestigious.'
translations.idiomatic: He resigned to mourn a parent, then was recalled to a seventh-rank post that was both important and prestigious. The relevant offices proposed him as registrar of Yong Prefecture. The emperor said: 'Important but not prestigious.'

sentences.zh: 復擬秘書郎，帝曰：「清而不要。」

translations.literal: They again proposed him as secretary; the emperor said: 'Prestigious but not important.'
translations.idiomatic: They next proposed him as secretary; the emperor said: 'Prestigious but not important.'

sentences.zh: 乃授侍御史。

translations.literal: He was then appointed attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，轉揚州大都督府司馬。

translations.literal: During Zhenguan, he was transferred to vice administrator of the Yangzhou Metropolitan Command.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenguan he was transferred to vice administrator of the Yangzhou Metropolitan Command.

sentences.zh: 初，突厥鐵勒部內附，即其地為瀚海都護府，詔素立領之。

translations.literal: At first, when the Tiele tribes of the Turks submitted allegiance, their territory was made the Hanhai Protectorate, and Suli was ordered to command it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tiele tribes of the Turks submitted, their territory was made the Hanhai Protectorate and Suli was ordered to command it.

sentences.zh: 於是，闕泥熟別部數梗邊，素立以不足用兵，遣使諭降，夷人感其惠，率馬牛以獻，素立止受酒一杯，歸其餘。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Quenisu branch repeatedly obstructed the frontier. Suli, deeming military force insufficient, sent envoys to persuade them to submit. The barbarians were moved by his kindness and led horses and cattle to offer in tribute; Suli accepted only one cup of wine and returned the rest.
translations.idiomatic: The Quenisu branch repeatedly harassed the frontier. Suli, deeming force insufficient, sent envoys to persuade them to submit. The tribes were moved by his kindness and brought horses and cattle as tribute; Suli accepted only one cup of wine and returned the rest.

sentences.zh: 乃開屯田，立署次，虜益畏威。

translations.literal: He then opened military colonies and established administrative posts; the barbarians increasingly feared his authority.
translations.idiomatic: He then opened military colonies and established administrative posts, and the tribes increasingly respected his authority.

sentences.zh: 歷太僕、鴻臚卿，累封高邑縣侯。

translations.literal: He served as minister of the imperial stud and minister of reception for foreign envoys, and was repeatedly enfeoffed as Marquis of Gaoyi County.
translations.idiomatic: He served as minister of the imperial stud and minister of reception for foreign envoys, and was repeatedly enfeoffed as Marquis of Gaoyi County.

sentences.zh: 出為綿州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as prefect of Mian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Mian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 永徽初，徙蒲州，將行，還所餘儲乞並什器於州，賫家書就道。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yonghui, he was transferred to Pu Prefecture. About to depart, he returned surplus stores and requested that utensils be left with the prefecture; he took only family letters on the road.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yonghui he was transferred to Pu Prefecture. Before departing, he returned surplus stores and left utensils with the prefecture, taking only family letters on the road.

sentences.zh: 會卒，高宗特廢朝一日，謚曰平。

translations.literal: He happened to die on the way; Emperor Gaozong specially suspended court for one day and posthumously titled him Ping.
translations.idiomatic: He died en route; Emperor Gaozong specially suspended court for one day and posthumously titled him Ping.

sentences.zh: 孫至遠，始名鵬。

translations.literal: His grandson Zhiyuan was originally named Peng.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Zhiyuan was originally named Peng.

sentences.zh: 而素立方奉使，謂家人曰：「古有待事名子，吾此役可命子孫矣。」

translations.literal: When Suli was about to go on a mission, he told his family: 'In antiquity there was the custom of naming a child after awaiting some event; this mission of mine can be used to name posterity.'
translations.idiomatic: When Suli was about to depart on a mission, he told his family: 'In antiquity children were named after awaited events; this mission of mine can be used to name posterity.'

sentences.zh: 遂以名之。

translations.literal: He was therefore given this name.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore given this name.

sentences.zh: 少秀晤，能治《尚書》、《左氏春秋》，未見杜預《釋例》而作《編記》，大趣略同。

translations.literal: In youth he was brilliant and quick; he mastered the Documents and Mr. Zuo's Spring and Autumn Annals. Without having seen Du Yu's Explanatory Examples, he wrote a Chronological Record whose general purport was largely the same.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was brilliant; he mastered the Documents and Mr. Zuo's Spring and Autumn Annals. Without having seen Du Yu's Explanatory Examples, he wrote a Chronological Record whose general approach was largely the same.

sentences.zh: 復撰《周書》，起後稷至赧，為傳紀，令狐德棻許其良史。

translations.literal: He also compiled a Book of Zhou, from Houji down to King Nan, in biographical and annal form; Linghu Defen acknowledged him as a good historian.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled a Book of Zhou from Houji down to King Nan in biographical and annal form; Linghu Defen acknowledged him as a fine historian.

sentences.zh: 始調蒲州參軍，累補乾封尉。

translations.literal: He was first assigned as aide of Pu Prefecture and was repeatedly promoted to assistant magistrate of Qianfeng.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as aide of Pu Prefecture and rose to assistant magistrate of Qianfeng.

sentences.zh: 上元時，制策高第，授明堂主簿。

translations.literal: In the Shangyuan era, he placed at the top of the policy-examination cohort and was appointed chief clerk of the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shangyuan era he ranked first in the policy examination and was appointed chief clerk of the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 以喪解，既除，調鴻臚主簿。

translations.literal: He resigned on account of mourning; once the mourning period ended, he was assigned as chief clerk of the Court of Reception.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned to mourn a parent and, once the mourning period ended, was assigned as chief clerk of the Court of Reception.

sentences.zh: 奏戎狄簿領，高宗悅，擢監察御史裏行。

translations.literal: He submitted a register of barbarian tribes; Emperor Gaozong was pleased and promoted him to acting investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a register of frontier tribes; Emperor Gaozong was pleased and promoted him to acting investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 忤貴幸，外遷，久乃歷司勛、吏部員外郎中。

translations.literal: He offended favored courtiers and was transferred outward; only after a long time did he serve successively as outer director in the Bureau of Merit and as outer director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He offended favored courtiers and was posted elsewhere; only after a long interval did he serve in the Bureau of Merit and as outer director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 遷天官侍郎，知選事，疾令史受賄謝，多所絀易，吏肅然斂手。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice minister of the Celestial Office and directed appointment affairs; he hated clerks who accepted bribes and favors, replaced many of them, and the officials soberly withdrew their hands.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice minister of the Celestial Office and directed appointments. He cracked down on clerks who took bribes and replaced many of them, and the staff soberly withdrew their hands.

sentences.zh: 有王忠者，被放，吏謬書其姓為「士」，欲擬訖增成之，至遠曰：「調者三萬，無士姓，此必王忠。」

translations.literal: There was a man named Wang Zhong who had been dismissed; a clerk mistakenly wrote his surname as 'Shi' and, intending to complete the draft afterward, Zhiyuan said: 'Among the thirty thousand appointees there is no surname Shi — this must be Wang Zhong.'
translations.idiomatic: A man named Wang Zhong had been dismissed, but a clerk mistakenly wrote his surname as Shi and planned to finish the draft later. Zhiyuan said: 'Among thirty thousand appointees there is no surname Shi — this must be Wang Zhong.'

sentences.zh: 吏叩頭服罪。

translations.literal: The clerk kowtowed and admitted guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The clerk kowtowed and admitted guilt.

sentences.zh: 至遠之知選，以內史李昭德進，人或勸其往謝，答曰：「公以公用我，奈何欲謝以私？」

translations.literal: When Zhiyuan took charge of appointments, it was through the recommendation of Chief Minister Li Zhaode; some urged him to go and offer thanks, but he replied: 'The lord employed me for public reasons — how could I wish to thank him for private reasons?'
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan owed his appointment to Chief Minister Li Zhaode; some urged him to go and offer thanks, but he replied: 'He employed me for public reasons — how could I thank him as a private favor?'

sentences.zh: 卒不詣。

translations.literal: In the end he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he never went.

sentences.zh: 故昭德銜之，出為壁州刺史。

translations.literal: Therefore Zhaode harbored resentment against him and had him sent out as prefect of Bi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaode therefore resented him and had him posted as prefect of Bi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 卒，年四十八。

translations.literal: He died at the age of forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 至遠父休烈，亦有文，終郪令，年四十九。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan's father Xiulie was also literary; he ended as magistrate of Qi and died at forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan's father Xiulie was also a man of letters; he ended his career as magistrate of Qi and died at forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 世嘆其父子材不盡雲。

translations.literal: The age lamented that father and son did not fully realize their talent.
translations.idiomatic: People lamented that father and son had not fully realized their talents.

sentences.zh: 至遠見桓彥範，力言其賢。

translations.literal: When Zhiyuan met Huan Yanfan, he strongly declared his worth.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhiyuan met Huan Yanfan, he strongly declared the man's worth.

sentences.zh: 盧從願尚少，高以評目。

translations.literal: Lu Congyuan was still young, yet Zhiyuan highly appraised him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Congyuan was still young, yet Zhiyuan rated him highly.

sentences.zh: 許弟從遠且貴，豫言其位，以驗所至。

translations.literal: He declared that his younger brother Congyuan would become eminent and foretold his rank, to verify how far his judgment reached.
translations.idiomatic: He declared that his younger brother Congyuan would rise to eminence and foretold his rank, to test the reach of his judgment.

sentences.zh: 蘇颋，其出也，少失母，至遠愛視甚謹，以女妻之。

translations.literal: Su Ting, a kinsman on his mother's side, lost his mother in youth; Zhiyuan cared for and watched over him with great care and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Su Ting, a maternal kinsman, lost his mother in youth; Zhiyuan cared for him with great devotion and gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 友兄弟，事寡姊有禮，世稱其德。

translations.literal: He was friendly with his brothers and treated his widowed elder sister with propriety; the age praised his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to his brothers and treated his widowed elder sister with proper respect; people praised his virtue.

sentences.zh: 從遠清密有學，神龍初，歷中書令、太府卿，累封趙郡公，謚曰懿。

translations.literal: Congyuan was pure, careful, and learned; at the beginning of Shenlong he served as chief minister of the Secretariat and minister of the imperial treasury, was repeatedly enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao Commandery, and was posthumously titled Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Congyuan was pure, careful, and learned. At the start of Shenlong he served as chief minister of the Secretariat and minister of the imperial treasury, was enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao Commandery, and was posthumously titled Yi.

sentences.zh: 兄弟皆德望相埒。

translations.literal: The brothers all matched one another in virtue and reputation.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers were all matched in virtue and reputation.

sentences.zh: 又從父遊道，武后時冬官尚書、同鳳閣鸞臺三品。

translations.literal: Their father's younger cousin Youdao, in Empress Wu's time, was minister of public works and third-rank associate of the Phoenix Pavilion and Luan Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Their father's younger cousin Youdao served under Empress Wu as minister of public works and third-rank associate of the Phoenix Pavilion and Luan Terrace.

sentences.zh: 至遠子畬，字玉田，少聰警。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan's son Yu, styled Yutian, was clever and alert in youth.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan's son Yu, styled Yutian, was clever and quick-witted in youth.

sentences.zh: 初歷汜水主簿，遇事蜂銳，雖廝豎，一閱輒記姓名、居業。

translations.literal: He first served as chief clerk of Sishui; in handling affairs he was sharp as a hornet — even a menial, once seen, he would remember name and occupation.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as chief clerk of Sishui. In handling affairs he was sharp as a hornet — even a menial, once seen, he would remember the person's name and occupation.

sentences.zh: 黜陟使路敬潛薦其清白，擢右臺監察御史裏行。

translations.literal: The promotion-and-demotion commissioner Lu Jingqian recommended his integrity and he was promoted to acting censor of the Right Platform.
translations.idiomatic: The promotion-and-demotion commissioner Lu Jingqian recommended his integrity, and he was promoted to acting censor of the Right Platform.

sentences.zh: 臺廢，授監察御史，累轉國子司業。

translations.literal: When the censorate was abolished, he was appointed investigating censor and was repeatedly transferred until he became vice director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: When the censorate was abolished, he was appointed investigating censor and eventually rose to vice director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 事母謹，累世同居，長幼有禮。

translations.literal: He served his mother carefully; for generations the family lived together, and elders and juniors observed propriety.
translations.idiomatic: He served his mother devotedly. For generations the family lived together, and elders and juniors observed proper decorum.

sentences.zh: 畬妻物故，時母病，恐悲傷，約家人無以哭聞母所，朝夕省侍無憂色。

translations.literal: Yu's wife died; at the time his mother was ill, fearing grief he instructed the household not to let weeping reach his mother's quarters; morning and evening he attended her without a sorrowful countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's wife died while his mother was ill. Fearing grief would harm her, he instructed the household not to let weeping reach her quarters and attended her morning and evening without a sorrowful face.

sentences.zh: 母終，毀而卒。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he wasted away in grief and died.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he wasted away in grief and died.

sentences.zh: 從遠子巖，年十餘歲，會中宗祀明堂，以近臣子弟執籩豆，巖進止中禮，授右宗衛兵曹參軍。

translations.literal: Congyuan's son Yan, in his teens, happened to attend when Emperor Zhongzong sacrificed at the Bright Hall; as a son of a close minister he bore the ritual vessels, and Yan's movements conformed to ritual propriety; he was appointed military officer of the Right Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Congyuan's son Yan, still in his teens, attended when Emperor Zhongzong sacrificed at the Bright Hall. As a son of a close minister he bore the ritual vessels, and Yan's movements were perfectly proper. He was appointed military officer of the Right Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 歷洛陽尉，累遷兵部郎中。

translations.literal: He served as aide of Luoyang and was repeatedly promoted to director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He served as aide of Luoyang and rose to director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 發扶風兵應姚、巂，稱旨，遷諫議大夫，封贊皇縣伯。

translations.literal: He mobilized Fufeng troops to support Yao and Yi prefectures; this pleased the emperor, and he was promoted to remonstrance grandee and enfeoffed as Earl of Zanhuang County.
translations.idiomatic: He mobilized Fufeng troops to support Yao and Yi prefectures. This pleased the emperor, and he was promoted to remonstrance grandee and enfeoffed as Earl of Zanhuang County.

sentences.zh: 終兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: He ended as vice minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 巖善草隸。

translations.literal: Yan was skilled in cursive and clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was skilled in cursive and clerical script.

sentences.zh: 為參軍時制一裘，服終身。

translations.literal: When he was a military aide he had one fur coat made and wore it all his life.
translations.idiomatic: As a military aide he had one fur coat made and wore it for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 薛大鼎，字重臣，蒲州汾陰人。

translations.literal: Xue Dading, styled Zhongchen, was a native of Fenyin in Pu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Dading, styled Zhongchen, was from Fenyin in Pu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父粹，為隋介州長史，與漢王諒同反，誅。

translations.literal: His father Cui served Sui as chief secretary of Jie Prefecture; he joined Prince of Han Liang in rebellion and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cui served the Sui as chief secretary of Jie Prefecture; he joined the Prince of Han, Liang, in rebellion and was executed.

sentences.zh: 大鼎貰為官奴，流辰州，用戰功得還。

translations.literal: Dading was ransomed as a government slave, was exiled to Chen Prefecture, and through military merit was able to return.
translations.idiomatic: Dading was ransomed from bondage as a government slave, was exiled to Chen Prefecture, and returned through military merit.

sentences.zh: 高祖兵興，謁見龍門，因說帝絕龍門，軍永豐倉就食，傳檄遠近，據天府，示豪桀，為拊背扼喉計，帝奇之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu raised his army, Dading met him at Longmen and urged him to block Longmen, march the army to the Ever-Abundant Granary for provisions, issue proclamations far and near, hold the granary of Heaven, display power to the bold, and adopt the strategy of patting the back while gripping the throat. The emperor marveled at this.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu raised his army, Dading met him at Longmen and urged him to block Longmen, march to the Ever-Abundant Granary for provisions, issue proclamations far and near, hold the imperial granary, display power to the bold, and adopt the strategy of patting the back while gripping the throat. The emperor marveled at this.

sentences.zh: 時諸將已決策先攻河東，故議置。

translations.literal: At the time the generals had already decided to attack Hedong first, so the proposal was set aside.
translations.idiomatic: The generals had already decided to attack Hedong first, so the proposal was set aside.

sentences.zh: 授大將軍府察非掾。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigator of wrongdoing in the grand general's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigator of wrongdoing in the grand general's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 出為山南道副大使，開屯田以實倉廩。

translations.literal: He went out as vice commissioner of the South Mountain Circuit and opened military colonies to fill the granaries.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as vice commissioner of the South Mountain Circuit and opened military colonies to fill the granaries.

sentences.zh: 趙郡王孝恭討輔公祏，以大鼎為饒州道軍師，引兵度彭蠡湖，以功遷浩州刺史。

translations.literal: When Prince of Zhao Commandery Xiaogong campaigned against Fu Gongshi, Dading served as military adviser on the Raozhou route, led troops across Lake Poyang, and for his merit was transferred to prefect of Hao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Zhao Commandery Xiaogong campaigned against Fu Gongshi, Dading served as military adviser on the Raozhou route, led troops across Lake Poyang, and for his merit was appointed prefect of Hao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 累徙滄州。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to Cang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was eventually transferred to Cang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 無棣渠久廞塞，大鼎浚治屬之海，商賈流行，裏民歌曰：「新溝通，舟楫利。

translations.literal: The Wudi Canal had long been silted and blocked; Dading dredged it and connected it to the sea; merchants traveled freely, and the people sang: 'The new channel is open, boats and oars prosper.
translations.idiomatic: The Wudi Canal had long been silted shut; Dading dredged it and connected it to the sea. Merchants traveled freely, and the people sang: 'The new channel is open, boats and oars prosper.

sentences.zh: 屬滄海，魚鹽至。

translations.literal: It reaches the blue sea, fish and salt arrive.
translations.idiomatic: It reaches the blue sea, fish and salt arrive.

sentences.zh: 昔徒行，今騁駟。

translations.literal: Once we walked on foot, now we gallop four-in-hand.
translations.idiomatic: Once we walked on foot, now we gallop in carriages.

sentences.zh: 美哉薛公德滂被！」

translations.literal: How fine is Lord Xue's virtue, spreading like a torrent!'
translations.idiomatic: How fine is Lord Xue's virtue, spreading like a torrent!'

sentences.zh: 又疏長蘆、漳、衡三渠，泄汙潦，水不為害。

translations.literal: He also dredged the three canals of Changlu, Zhang, and Heng to drain stagnant floodwater so that water no longer caused harm.
translations.idiomatic: He also dredged the Changlu, Zhang, and Heng canals to drain stagnant floodwater so that water no longer caused harm.

sentences.zh: 是時，鄭德本在瀛州，賈敦頤為冀州，皆有治名故河北稱「鐺腳刺史」。

translations.literal: At this time Zheng Deben was in Ying Prefecture and Jia Dunyi was in Ji Prefecture; all had reputations for good governance, so north of the Yellow River they were called the 'Tripod-Leg Prefects.'
translations.idiomatic: At this time Zheng Deben was in Ying Prefecture and Jia Dunyi in Ji Prefecture; all were famed for good governance, so north of the Yellow River they were called the 'Tripod-Leg Prefects.'

sentences.zh: 永徽中，遷銀青光祿大夫，行荊州大都督長史。

translations.literal: In the Yonghui era he was transferred to silver-blue-glow grand master of splendid happiness and acting chief administrator of the Jingzhou Metropolitan Command.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yonghui era he was promoted to silver-blue-glow grand master of splendid happiness and acting chief administrator of the Jingzhou Metropolitan Command.

sentences.zh: 卒，謚曰恭。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously titled Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously titled Gong.

sentences.zh: 子克構，有器識，永隆初，歷戶部郎中。

translations.literal: His son Kegou had capacity and insight; at the beginning of Yonglong he served as director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kegou had capacity and insight; at the start of Yonglong he served as director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 族人黃門侍郎顗，以弟紹尚太平公主，問於克構，答曰：「室有傲婦，善士所惡。

translations.literal: His clansman Huangmen Attendant Yi, because his younger brother Shao was betrothed to Princess Taiping, asked Kegou, who replied: 'A household with a haughty wife is what good men detest.
translations.idiomatic: His clansman Huangmen Attendant Yi, whose younger brother Shao was betrothed to Princess Taiping, asked Kegou, who replied: 'A household with a haughty wife is what good men detest.

sentences.zh: 夫惟淑德，以配君子，無患可矣。」

translations.literal: Only virtuous character, to match a gentleman — then there is nothing to worry about.'
translations.idiomatic: Only virtuous character, to match a gentleman — then there is nothing to worry about.'

sentences.zh: 顗不敢沮，而紹卒誅。

translations.literal: Yi did not dare dissuade him, and Shao was eventually executed.
translations.idiomatic: Yi did not dare dissuade him, and Shao was eventually executed.

sentences.zh: 陳思忠居父喪，詔奪服，客往吊，思忠辭以辰日不見。

translations.literal: Chen Sizhong was in mourning for his father when an edict ordered him to leave mourning garb; when a guest came to offer condolences, Sizhong declined on the ground that it was a chen day on which he did not receive visitors.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Sizhong was mourning his father when an edict ordered him to leave mourning garb. When a guest came to offer condolences, Sizhong declined on the ground that it was a chen day on which he did not receive visitors.

sentences.zh: 克構曰：「事親者，避嫌可也；

translations.literal: Kegou said: 'In serving parents, one may avoid suspicion;
translations.idiomatic: Kegou said: 'In serving parents, one may avoid suspicion;

sentences.zh: 既孤矣，則無不哭。」

translations.literal: but once one is orphaned, there is no not weeping.'
translations.idiomatic: but once one is orphaned, one cannot refrain from weeping.'

sentences.zh: 世服其言。

translations.literal: The age admired his words.
translations.idiomatic: People admired his words.

sentences.zh: 天授中，遷麟臺監。

translations.literal: In the Tianshou era he was transferred to director of the Forest Platform.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianshou era he was transferred to director of the Forest Platform.

sentences.zh: 坐弟為酷吏所陷，流死嶺南。

translations.literal: Because his younger brother was framed by a harsh official, he was exiled and died in Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Because his younger brother was framed by a harsh official, he was exiled and died in Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 賈敦頤，曹州冤句人。

translations.literal: Jia Dunyi was a native of Yuanqu in Cao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Dunyi was from Yuanqu in Cao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 貞觀時，數歷州刺史，資廉潔。

translations.literal: During Zhenguan he served repeatedly as prefect of several prefectures; his character was honest and clean.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenguan he served repeatedly as prefect; his character was honest and incorruptible.

sentences.zh: 入朝，常盡室行，車一乘，弊甚，羸馬繩羈，道上不知其刺史也。

translations.literal: When he came to court he usually traveled with his whole household in one carriage, very worn; a thin horse with rope reins — on the road no one knew he was a prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to court he usually traveled with his whole household in one very worn carriage, a thin horse with rope reins — on the road no one knew he was a prefect.

sentences.zh: 久之，為洛州司馬，以公累下獄，太宗貰之，有司執不貰，帝曰：「人孰無過，吾去太甚者。

translations.literal: After a long time he served as vice prefect of Luo Prefecture; because of a public offense he was imprisoned. Emperor Taizong pardoned him, but the relevant offices insisted on not pardoning. The emperor said: 'Who has no faults? I remove the excessive ones.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he served as vice prefect of Luo Prefecture and was imprisoned for a public offense. Emperor Taizong pardoned him, but the relevant offices refused. The emperor said: 'Who has no faults? I remove the excessive ones.

sentences.zh: 若悉繩以法，雖子不得於父，況臣得事其君乎？」

translations.literal: If all were bound strictly by law, even a son could not serve his father — how much less could a minister serve his lord?'
translations.idiomatic: If all were bound strictly by law, even a son could not serve his father — how much less could a minister serve his lord?'

sentences.zh: 遂獲原。

translations.literal: He was then pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: He was then pardoned.

sentences.zh: 徙瀛州刺史，州瀕滹沱、滱二水，歲湓溢，壞室廬，浸洳數百里。

translations.literal: He was transferred to prefect of Ying Prefecture; the prefecture bordered the Hutuo and Hu rivers, which overflowed each year, destroying houses and soaking several hundred li of land.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to prefect of Ying Prefecture, which bordered the Hutuo and Hu rivers. Each year they overflowed, destroying houses and soaking land for hundreds of li.

sentences.zh: 敦頤為立堰庸，水不能暴，百姓利之。

translations.literal: Dunyi built dikes and labor corvée for the people; the water could not rage violently, and the common people benefited.
translations.idiomatic: Dunyi built dikes and organized labor corvée; the floods could no longer rage, and the people benefited.

sentences.zh: 時弟敦實為饒陽令，政清靜，吏民嘉美。

translations.literal: At the time his younger brother Dunshi was magistrate of Raoyang; his governance was clear and quiet, and officials and people praised it.
translations.idiomatic: At the time his younger brother Dunshi was magistrate of Raoyang; his governance was clear and quiet, and officials and people praised it.

sentences.zh: 舊制，大功之嫌不連官，朝廷以其兄弟治行相高，故不徙以示寵。

translations.literal: By old regulation, relatives within greater mourning were not posted to connected offices; the court, because the brothers' governing conduct was equally high, did not transfer them to show favor.
translations.idiomatic: By old regulation, relatives within greater mourning were not posted to connected offices; because the brothers' governing conduct was equally outstanding, the court did not transfer them, as a mark of favor.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，遷洛州。

translations.literal: In the Yonghui era he was transferred to Luo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yonghui era he was transferred to Luo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 洛多豪右，占田類逾制，敦頤舉沒者三千餘頃，以賦貧民，發奸擿伏，下無能欺。

translations.literal: Luoyang had many powerful families whose occupied land mostly exceeded regulations; Dunyi reported and confiscated more than three thousand qing, assigning it to the poor; he exposed hidden wrongdoing, and subordinates could not deceive him.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang had many powerful families whose landholdings mostly exceeded regulations. Dunyi confiscated more than three thousand qing and assigned it to the poor. He exposed hidden wrongdoing, and subordinates could not deceive him.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 咸亨初，敦實為洛州長史，亦寬惠，人心懷向。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianheng, Dunshi served as chief administrator of Luo Prefecture; he too was lenient and benevolent, and people's hearts turned toward him.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Xianheng, Dunshi served as chief administrator of Luo Prefecture. He too was lenient and benevolent, and the people turned toward him.

sentences.zh: 洛陽令楊德幹矜酷烈，杖殺人以立威，敦實喻止，曰：「政在養人，傷生過多，雖能，不足貴也。」

translations.literal: The magistrate of Luoyang, Yang Degan, was harsh and cruel; he beat people to death to establish authority. Dunshi admonished him to stop, saying: 'Government lies in nurturing the people; if lives harmed are too many, even if one has ability, it is not worth esteem.'
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate of Luoyang, Yang Degan, was harsh and cruel and beat people to death to establish authority. Dunshi admonished him to stop, saying: 'Government lies in nurturing the people; if too many lives are harmed, even ability is not worth esteem.'

sentences.zh: 德幹為衰減。

translations.literal: Degan somewhat reduced his severity.
translations.idiomatic: Degan somewhat reduced his severity.

sentences.zh: 始，洛人為敦頤刻碑大市旁，及敦實入為太子右庶子，人復為立碑其側，故號「常棣碑」。

translations.literal: At first the people of Luoyang erected a stele for Dunyi beside the great market; when Dunshi entered service as right vice tutor of the heir apparent, the people again erected a stele beside it, hence the name 'Stelae of the Evergreen Privet.'
translations.idiomatic: At first the people of Luoyang erected a stele for Dunyi beside the great market. When Dunshi entered service as right vice tutor of the heir apparent, they erected another beside it, hence the name 'Stelae of the Evergreen Privet.'

sentences.zh: 歷懷州刺史，有美跡。

translations.literal: He served as prefect of Huai Prefecture and left fine traces of governance.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Huai Prefecture and left a fine record of governance.

sentences.zh: 永淳初致仕，病篤，子孫迎醫，敦實不肯見，曰：「未聞良醫能治老也。」

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongchun he retired; when gravely ill, his sons and grandsons summoned a physician, but Dunshi refused to see him, saying: 'I have never heard that a good physician can cure old age.'
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yongchun he retired. When gravely ill, his sons and grandsons summoned a physician, but Dunshi refused to see him, saying: 'I have never heard that a good physician can cure old age.'

sentences.zh: 卒，年九十餘。

translations.literal: He died at more than ninety.
translations.idiomatic: He died at more than ninety.

sentences.zh: 子膺福，左散騎常侍、昭文館學士，以竇懷貞黨誅。

translations.literal: His son Yingfu was left attendant cavalryman-at-large and scholar of the Zhaowen Hall; he was executed as a member of Dou Huaizhen's faction.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yingfu was left attendant cavalryman-at-large and scholar of the Zhaowen Hall; he was executed as a member of Dou Huaizhen's faction.

sentences.zh: 德幹歷澤、齊、汴、相四州刺史，有威嚴＃急語曰：「寧食三斗炭，不逢楊德幹。」

translations.literal: Degan served successively as prefect of Ze, Qi, Bian, and Xiang prefectures; he had formidable authority. A saying ran: 'Better eat three pecks of charcoal than encounter Yang Degan.'
translations.idiomatic: Degan served successively as prefect of Ze, Qi, Bian, and Xiang prefectures and had formidable authority. A saying ran: 'Better eat three pecks of charcoal than encounter Yang Degan.'

sentences.zh: 天授初，子神讓與徐敬業起兵，皆及誅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianshou, his son Shenrang joined Xu Jingye in raising troops; both were executed.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tianshou, his son Shenrang joined Xu Jingye in raising troops; both were executed.

sentences.zh: 田仁會，雍州長安人。

translations.literal: Tian Renhui was a native of Chang'an in Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Renhui was from Chang'an in Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖軌，隋幽州刺史，封信都郡公。

translations.literal: His grandfather Gui served Sui as prefect of You Prefecture and was enfeoffed as Duke of Xindu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Gui served the Sui as prefect of You Prefecture and was enfeoffed as Duke of Xindu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 父弘襲封，至陵州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Hong inherited the enfeoffment and rose to prefect of Ling Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hong inherited the enfeoffment and rose to prefect of Ling Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 仁會擢制舉，仕累左武候中郎將。

translations.literal: Renhui passed the policy examination and served successively as middle general of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Renhui passed the policy examination and rose to middle general of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 太宗征遼東，而薛延陀以數萬騎掩河內，詔仁會與執失思力率兵擊敗之，尾逐數百里，延陀幾生得，璽書嘉尉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong campaigned in Liaodong, Xueyantuo with tens of thousands of horsemen raided Henei; Renhui was ordered with Zhisi Sili to lead troops and defeat them, pursuing for several hundred li; Xueyantuo was nearly captured alive; an imperial letter praised and comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong campaigned in Liaodong, Xueyantuo raided Henei with tens of thousands of horsemen. Renhui was ordered with Zhisi Sili to lead troops and defeat them, pursuing for hundreds of li. Xueyantuo was nearly captured alive, and an imperial letter praised him.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，為平州刺史，歲旱，自暴以祈，而雨大至，谷遂登。

translations.literal: In the Yonghui era he served as prefect of Ping Prefecture; in a year of drought he exposed himself to the sun to pray, and great rain came; the grain then ripened.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yonghui era he served as prefect of Ping Prefecture. In a year of drought he exposed himself to the sun in prayer, great rain came, and the grain ripened.

sentences.zh: 人歌曰：「父母育我兮田使君，挺精誠兮上天聞，中田致雨兮山出雲，倉廩實兮禮義申，願君常在兮不患貧。」

translations.literal: The people sang: 'Our parents nourished us — Prefect Tian! With utmost sincerity Heaven heard; in the fields rain came and clouds rose from the mountains; granaries are full and ritual and righteousness flourish; may the lord always remain — then we need not fear poverty.'
translations.idiomatic: The people sang: 'Our parents nourished us — Prefect Tian! With utmost sincerity Heaven heard; rain came to the fields and clouds rose from the mountains; granaries are full and ritual and righteousness flourish; may you always remain — then we need not fear poverty.'

sentences.zh: 五遷勝州都督，境有夙賊，依山剽行人，仁會發騎捕格，夷之。

translations.literal: After five transfers he became military commissioner of Sheng Prefecture; in the territory were longstanding bandits who plundered travelers from the mountains; Renhui dispatched cavalry to capture and kill them, exterminating them.
translations.idiomatic: After five transfers he became military commissioner of Sheng Prefecture. Longstanding bandits in the territory plundered travelers from the mountains; Renhui dispatched cavalry to capture and kill them, exterminating the threat.

sentences.zh: 城門夜開，道無寇跡。

translations.literal: City gates were opened at night; on the roads there were no traces of bandits.
translations.idiomatic: City gates were opened at night, and the roads showed no trace of bandits.

sentences.zh: 入為太府少卿，遷右金吾將軍。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as vice director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury and was transferred to general of the Right Golden Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as vice director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury and was transferred to general of the Right Golden Guard.

sentences.zh: 所得祿，估有贏，輒入之官，人以為尚名。

translations.literal: When his salary, once appraised, showed a surplus, he immediately turned it in to the government; people thought he valued reputation.
translations.idiomatic: When his salary, once appraised, showed a surplus, he immediately turned it in to the government; people thought he valued reputation.

sentences.zh: 然資強摯疾惡，晝夜循行，有絲毫奸必發，廷中謫罰日數百，京師無貴賤舉憚之。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was strong, upright, and hated evil; day and night he patrolled; the slightest wrongdoing he always exposed; in court demotions and punishments numbered in the hundreds each day; in the capital none, high or low, failed to fear him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet by nature he was strong, upright, and hated evil. Day and night he patrolled; the slightest wrongdoing he exposed. Court demotions and punishments numbered in the hundreds each day, and in the capital none, high or low, failed to fear him.

sentences.zh: 巫傳鬼道惑眾，自言能活死人，市裏尊神，仁會劾徙於邊。

translations.literal: A shaman spread ghostly ways to delude the masses, claiming he could revive the dead; the market district honored him as a god; Renhui impeached him and had him exiled to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: A shaman spread ghostly ways to delude the masses, claiming he could revive the dead. The market district honored him as a god; Renhui impeached him and had him exiled to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 轉右衛將軍，以年老乞骸骨。

translations.literal: He was transferred to general of the Right Guard and, on account of old age, requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to general of the Right Guard and, on account of old age, requested retirement.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十八，謚曰威。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-eight and was posthumously titled Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-eight and was posthumously titled Wei.

sentences.zh: 子歸道，明經及第，累擢通事舍人內供奉、左衛郎將。

translations.literal: His son Guidao passed the classics examination and was repeatedly promoted to palace attendant for foreign affairs and left guard commandant.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guidao passed the classics examination and rose to palace attendant for foreign affairs and left guard commandant.

sentences.zh: 突厥默啜請和，武后詔將軍閻知微冊可汗號，持節往。

translations.literal: The Turk Moqochuo requested peace; Empress Wu ordered General Yan Zhiwei to invest him with the title of khan and sent him bearing credentials.
translations.idiomatic: The Turk Moqochuo requested peace; Empress Wu ordered General Yan Zhiwei to invest him with the title of khan and sent him bearing credentials.

sentences.zh: 默啜又遣使謝，知微遇諸道，即與緋袍銀帶，因表使者即到，請備禮廷賜。

translations.literal: Moqochuo again sent envoys to express thanks; Zhiwei, meeting them on the road, immediately gave them scarlet robes and silver belts, and memorialized that the envoys had already arrived, requesting that full court ceremony be prepared to bestow gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Moqochuo again sent envoys to express thanks. Zhiwei, meeting them on the road, immediately gave them scarlet robes and silver belts and memorialized that the envoys had arrived, requesting full court ceremony to bestow gifts.

sentences.zh: 歸道諫曰：「虜背惠且積年，今悔過入朝，解辮削衽宜待天旨。

translations.literal: Guidao remonstrated, saying: 'The barbarians have betrayed kindness for years; now that they repent and come to court, loosening braids and cutting robes should await Heaven's command.
translations.idiomatic: Guidao remonstrated: 'The barbarians have betrayed our kindness for years. Now that they repent and come to court, loosening braids and cutting robes should await the emperor's command.

sentences.zh: 而知微擅賜，使朝廷何以加之？

translations.literal: Yet Zhiwei bestows gifts on his own authority — how can the court add further honors?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhiwei bestows gifts on his own authority — what further honors can the court add?

sentences.zh: 宜敕初服，須天子命。

translations.literal: Initial robes should be granted by edict and require the Son of Heaven's command.
translations.idiomatic: Initial robes should be granted by edict and require the emperor's command.

sentences.zh: 小國使者，不足備禮迓之。」

translations.literal: Envoys from a small state do not warrant full ceremony to receive them.'
translations.idiomatic: Envoys from a small state do not warrant full ceremony to receive them.'

sentences.zh: 後從焉。

translations.literal: Later he followed on the mission.
translations.idiomatic: Later he accompanied the mission.

sentences.zh: 默啜將至單于都護府，詔歸道攝司賓卿往勞。

translations.literal: When Moqochuo was about to reach the Chanyu Protectorate, Guidao was ordered to serve as acting minister of reception and go to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When Moqochuo was about to reach the Chanyu Protectorate, Guidao was ordered to serve as acting minister of reception and go to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 默啜請六胡州及都護府地不得，大怨望，執歸道將害之。

translations.literal: Moqochuo's request for the Six Hu Prefectures and the protectorate territory was denied; he was greatly resentful, seized Guidao, and was about to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Moqochuo's request for the Six Hu Prefectures and the protectorate territory was denied. Greatly resentful, he seized Guidao and was about to kill him.

sentences.zh: 歸道色不橈，詈且讓，為陳禍福，默啜亦悔。

translations.literal: Guidao's countenance did not waver; he cursed and reproached him, explained fortune and disaster, and Moqochuo also repented.
translations.idiomatic: Guidao's countenance did not waver. He cursed and reproached him, explained fortune and disaster, and Moqochuo repented.

sentences.zh: 會有詔賜默啜粟三萬石，彩五萬段，農器三千，且許結婚，於是更以禮遣歸道。

translations.literal: It happened that an edict granted Moqochuo thirty thousand shi of grain, fifty thousand bolts of silk, three thousand farming tools, and permission for marriage alliance; thereupon he sent Guidao away with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then granted Moqochuo thirty thousand shi of grain, fifty thousand bolts of silk, three thousand farming tools, and permission for marriage alliance. Moqochuo then sent Guidao away with ceremony.

sentences.zh: 既還，具陳默啜不臣狀，請備邊。

translations.literal: Once returned, he fully reported Moqochuo's disloyal conduct and requested border preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Once returned, he fully reported Moqochuo's disloyal conduct and requested border preparations.

sentences.zh: 已而果反，乃擢歸道夏官侍郎，益親信。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Moqochuo did rebel; Guidao was then promoted to vice minister of the Summer Office and gained greater trust.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Moqochuo rebelled as predicted. Guidao was promoted to vice minister of the Summer Office and gained greater trust.

sentences.zh: 遷左金吾將軍、司膳卿，押千騎宿衛玄武門。

translations.literal: He was transferred to general of the Left Golden Guard and minister of provisions, commanding a thousand horsemen to guard the Xuanwu Gate by night.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to general of the Left Golden Guard and minister of provisions, commanding a thousand horsemen to guard the Xuanwu Gate by night.

sentences.zh: 桓彥範等誅二張，而歸道不豫聞，及索騎士，拒不應。

translations.literal: When Huan Yanfan and others executed the Two Zhangs, Guidao had not been informed in advance; when they demanded horsemen, he refused to respond.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Yanfan and others executed the Two Zhangs, Guidao had not been informed in advance. When they demanded horsemen, he refused to respond.

sentences.zh: 事平，彥範欲誅之，以辭直，免，還私第。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, Yanfan wished to execute him, but because his words were upright he was spared and returned to his private residence.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was settled, Yanfan wished to execute him, but because his words were upright he was spared and returned home.

sentences.zh: 然中宗壯其守，召拜太僕少卿，遷殿中少監、右金吾將軍。

translations.literal: Yet Emperor Zhongzong admired his integrity, summoned and appointed him vice director of the imperial stud, and transferred him to vice director of the palace workshops and general of the Right Golden Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Emperor Zhongzong admired his integrity, summoned him as vice director of the imperial stud, and transferred him to vice director of the palace workshops and general of the Right Golden Guard.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈輔國大將軍，追封原國公，謚曰烈，帝自為文以祭。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made grand general who assists the state, enfeoffed as Duke of Yuan State, and titled Lie; the emperor himself composed a text to offer sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made grand general who assists the state, enfeoffed as Duke of Yuan State, and titled Lie. The emperor himself composed a text to offer sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 子賓庭，開元時至光祿卿。

translations.literal: His son Binting, in the Kaiyuan era, rose to minister of the imperial household.
translations.idiomatic: His son Binting rose to minister of the imperial household in the Kaiyuan era.

sentences.zh: 裴懷古，壽州壽春人。

translations.literal: Pei Huaigu was a native of Shouchun in Shou Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Huaigu was from Shouchun in Shou Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳中，上書闕下，補下邽主簿，頻遷監察御史。

translations.literal: In the Yifeng era he submitted a memorial at the palace gate, was appointed chief clerk of Xiagui, and was frequently promoted to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yifeng era he submitted a memorial at the palace gate, was appointed chief clerk of Xiagui, and rose to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 姚、巂道蠻反，命懷古馳驛往懷輯之，申明誅賞，歸者日千計。

translations.literal: The barbarians of the Yao and Yi routes rebelled; Huaigu was ordered to ride post-haste to soothe and gather them, clarifying punishments and rewards; those who submitted numbered a thousand per day.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians of the Yao and Yi routes rebelled. Huaigu was ordered to ride post-haste to soothe and gather them, clarifying punishments and rewards. Those who submitted numbered a thousand per day.

sentences.zh: 俄縛首惡，遂定南方，蠻夏立石著功。

translations.literal: Soon he bound the chief culprits and pacified the south; barbarians and Chinese alike erected steles recording his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he bound the chief culprits and pacified the south. Barbarians and Chinese alike erected steles recording his achievements.

sentences.zh: 恒州浮屠為其徒誣告祝詛不道，武后怒，命按誅之。

translations.literal: A Buddhist monk in Heng Prefecture was falsely accused by his disciples of cursing with impious rites; Empress Wu was angry and ordered investigation and execution.
translations.idiomatic: A Buddhist monk in Heng Prefecture was falsely accused by his disciples of cursing with impious rites. Empress Wu was angry and ordered investigation and execution.

sentences.zh: 懷古得其枉，為後申訴，不聽，因曰：「陛下法與天下畫一，豈使臣殺無辜以希盛旨哉？

translations.literal: Huaigu found the injustice and appealed on the monk's behalf; he was not heeded, and therefore said: 'Your Majesty's law is one with all under Heaven — how could you have me kill the innocent to seek your supreme intent?
translations.idiomatic: Huaigu found the injustice and appealed on the monk's behalf but was not heeded. He said: 'Your Majesty's law is one with all under Heaven — how could you have me kill the innocent to please you?

sentences.zh: 即其人有不臣狀，臣何情寬之？」

translations.literal: If the man truly showed disloyal conduct, why would I wish to spare him?'
