translations.idiomatic: If the man truly showed disloyal conduct, why would I wish to spare him?'

sentences.zh: 後意解，得不誅。

translations.literal: Later her anger eased and he was not executed.
translations.idiomatic: Later her anger eased and the monk was not executed.

sentences.zh: 閻知微之使突厥，懷古監其軍。

translations.literal: When Yan Zhiwei went as envoy to the Turks, Huaigu supervised his escort.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Zhiwei went as envoy to the Turks, Huaigu supervised his escort.

sentences.zh: 默啜脅知微稱可汗，又欲官懷古，不肯拜，將殺之。

translations.literal: Moqochuo coerced Zhiwei to proclaim him khan and also wished to appoint Huaigu to office; Huaigu refused to bow and was about to be killed.
translations.idiomatic: Moqochuo coerced Zhiwei to proclaim him khan and also wished to appoint Huaigu to office. Huaigu refused to bow and was about to be killed.

sentences.zh: 辭曰：「守忠而死與毀節以生敦與？

translations.literal: He replied: 'Which is weightier — dying while keeping loyalty, or living while destroying integrity?
translations.idiomatic: He replied: 'Which is weightier — dying while keeping loyalty, or living while destroying integrity?

sentences.zh: 請就斬，不避也。」

translations.literal: I request immediate execution and will not shrink from it.'
translations.idiomatic: I request immediate execution and will not shrink from it.'

sentences.zh: 遂囚軍中，因得亡，而素尫弱，不能騎，宛轉山谷間，僅達并州。

translations.literal: He was then imprisoned in the army camp but managed to escape; by nature he was frail and weak and could not ride; winding through valleys and mountains, he barely reached Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was imprisoned in the army camp but managed to escape. Frail by nature and unable to ride, he wound through valleys and mountains and barely reached Bing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時長史武重規縱暴，左右妄殺人取賞，見懷古至，爭執之。

translations.literal: At the time Chief Administrator Wu Chonggui was violent and unrestrained; his attendants killed people at random for rewards; seeing Huaigu arrive, they competed to seize him.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Administrator Wu Chonggui was violent and unrestrained; his attendants killed people at random for rewards. Seeing Huaigu arrive, they competed to seize him.

sentences.zh: 有果毅嘗識懷古，疾呼曰：「裴御史也。」

translations.literal: A resolute guard who had once known Huaigu cried out urgently: 'It is Censor Pei.'
translations.idiomatic: A resolute guard who had once known Huaigu cried out urgently: 'It is Censor Pei.'

sentences.zh: 遂免。

translations.literal: He was then spared.
translations.idiomatic: He was then spared.

sentences.zh: 遷祠部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to outer director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to outer director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 姚、巂酋等叩闕下，願得懷古鎮安遠夷，拜姚州都督，以疾辭。

translations.literal: Chieftains of Yao and Yi came to the palace gate, wishing to have Huaigu pacify the distant barbarians; he was appointed military commissioner of Yao Prefecture but declined on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Chieftains of Yao and Yi came to the palace gate, wishing to have Huaigu pacify the distant barbarians. He was appointed military commissioner of Yao Prefecture but declined on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 始安賊歐陽倩眾數萬，剽沒州縣，以懷古為桂州都督招尉討擊使，未逾嶺，逆以書諭禍福，賊迎降，自陳為吏侵而反。

translations.literal: The bandit Ouyang Qian of Shian had tens of thousands of followers and plundered prefectures and counties; Huaigu was made military commissioner of Gui Prefecture with authority to recruit, pacify, and attack; before crossing the ridge, he sent a letter in advance explaining fortune and disaster; the bandits came to welcome his surrender, confessing they had rebelled because officials oppressed them.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit Ouyang Qian of Shian had tens of thousands of followers and plundered prefectures and counties. Huaigu was made military commissioner of Gui Prefecture with authority to recruit, pacify, and attack. Before crossing the ridge, he sent a letter explaining fortune and disaster. The bandits came to surrender, confessing they had rebelled because officials oppressed them.

sentences.zh: 懷古知其誠，以為示不疑，可破其謀，乃輕騎赴之。

translations.literal: Huaigu knew their sincerity and thought that showing no suspicion could break their plot; he therefore went with a light escort.
translations.idiomatic: Huaigu knew their sincerity and thought that showing trust could break their plot. He went with a light escort.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「獠夷難親，備之且不信，況易之哉！」

translations.literal: Someone said: 'Liao barbarians are hard to approach — if you prepare against them they will not trust you; how much less if you treat them lightly!'
translations.idiomatic: Someone said: 'Liao barbarians are hard to approach — if you prepare against them they will not trust you; how much less if you treat them lightly!'

sentences.zh: 答曰：「忠信可通神明，況裔人耶！」

translations.literal: He replied: 'Loyalty and trust can reach the spirits — how much more frontier peoples!'
translations.idiomatic: He replied: 'Loyalty and trust can reach the spirits — how much more frontier peoples!'

sentences.zh: 身至壁撫諭，倩等大喜，悉歸所掠出降，雖諸洞素翻覆者，亦牽連根附，嶺外平。

translations.literal: He went in person to the stockade to soothe and instruct; Qian and the others were greatly pleased, returned all they had plundered, and came out to surrender; even caves that had always been fickle were drawn in and attached; south of the ridges was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He went in person to the stockade to soothe and instruct. Qian and the others were greatly pleased, returned all they had plundered, and surrendered. Even caves that had always been fickle were drawn in, and the region south of the ridges was pacified.

sentences.zh: 徙相州刺史、并州大都督長史，所至吏民懷愛。

translations.literal: He was transferred to prefect of Xiang Prefecture and chief administrator of the Bingzhou Metropolitan Command; wherever he went officials and people cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to prefect of Xiang Prefecture and chief administrator of the Bingzhou Metropolitan Command. Wherever he went, officials and people cherished him.

sentences.zh: 神龍中，召為左羽林大將軍，未至官，還為并州。

translations.literal: In the Shenlong era he was summoned as grand general of the Left Forest Guard; before reaching office he was returned to Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shenlong era he was summoned as grand general of the Left Forest Guard but, before reaching office, was returned to Bing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 人知其還，攜扶老稚出迎。

translations.literal: When people learned of his return, they brought out the old and young to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When people learned of his return, they brought out the old and young to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 崔宣道始代為長史，亦野次。

translations.literal: Cui Xuandao had just replaced him as chief administrator and was also encamped in the countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xuandao had just replaced him as chief administrator and was also encamped in the countryside.

sentences.zh: 懷古不欲厚愧宣道，使人驅迎者還，而來者愈眾，得人心類如此。

translations.literal: Huaigu did not wish to deeply shame Xuandao and had the welcomers driven back, yet those who came grew ever more numerous — winning people's hearts was like this.
translations.idiomatic: Huaigu did not wish to deeply shame Xuandao and had the welcomers driven back, yet those who came grew ever more numerous — such was his way of winning hearts.

sentences.zh: 俄轉幽州都督，綏懷兩蕃，將舉落內屬，會以左威衛大將軍召，而孫佺代之，而佺不知兵，遂敗其師。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to military commissioner of You Prefecture, soothing and winning over the two barbarian tribes; he was about to bring their settlements to submit when he was summoned as grand general of the Left Martial Guard; Sun Quan replaced him, and Quan did not understand warfare, so the army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to military commissioner of You Prefecture, soothing the two barbarian tribes. He was about to bring their settlements to submit when he was summoned as grand general of the Left Martial Guard. Sun Quan replaced him, but Quan did not understand warfare and the army was defeated.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 懷古清介審慎，在幽州時，韓琬以監察御史監軍，稱其「馭士信，臨財廉，國名將」云。

translations.literal: Huaigu was pure, upright, and careful; when in You Prefecture, Han Wan, serving as investigating censor supervising the army, praised him as 'commanding men with trust, facing wealth with integrity — a renowned general of the state.'
translations.idiomatic: Huaigu was pure, upright, and careful. When in You Prefecture, Han Wan, serving as investigating censor supervising the army, praised him as 'commanding men with trust, facing wealth with integrity — a renowned general of the state.'

sentences.zh: 韋景駿，司農少卿弘機孫。

translations.literal: Wei Jingjun was the grandson of Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue Hongji.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jingjun was the grandson of Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue Hongji.

sentences.zh: 中明經。

translations.literal: He passed the illuminated classics examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the illuminated classics examination.

sentences.zh: 神龍中，歷肥鄉令。

translations.literal: In the Shenlong era he served as magistrate of Feixiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shenlong era he served as magistrate of Feixiang.

sentences.zh: 縣北瀕漳，連年泛溢，人苦之。

translations.literal: The county bordered the Zhang River to the north; year after year it overflowed, and the people suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: The county bordered the Zhang River to the north, which overflowed year after year and caused the people great suffering.

sentences.zh: 舊防迫漕渠，雖峭岸，隨即壞決。

translations.literal: The old dikes pressed close to the canal channel; though the banks were steep, they immediately broke and burst.
translations.idiomatic: The old dikes pressed close to the canal channel; though the banks were steep, they immediately broke and burst.

sentences.zh: 景駿相地勢，益南千步，因高築鄣，水至堤趾輒去，其北燥為腴田。

translations.literal: Jingjun surveyed the terrain, extended southward a thousand paces, and built embankments on high ground; when water reached the foot of the dike it immediately departed, and the land to the north dried into fertile fields.
translations.idiomatic: Jingjun surveyed the terrain, extended southward a thousand paces, and built embankments on high ground. When water reached the foot of the dike it immediately departed, and the land to the north dried into fertile fields.

sentences.zh: 又維艚以梁其上，而廢長橋，功少費約，後遂為法。

translations.literal: He also moored boats to bridge above it and abolished the long bridge; the work was less and the expense modest, and afterward this became the standard method.
translations.idiomatic: He also moored boats to bridge above it and abolished the long bridge. The work was less and the expense modest, and afterward this became the standard method.

sentences.zh: 方河北饑，身巡閭里，勸人通有無，教導撫循，縣民獨免流散。

translations.literal: Just as Hebei was suffering famine, he personally toured the villages, encouraged people to share what they had, instructed and comforted them, and the county's people alone were spared scattering and displacement.
translations.idiomatic: Just as Hebei was suffering famine, he personally toured the villages, encouraged people to share what they had, and instructed and comforted them. The county's people alone were spared scattering and displacement.

sentences.zh: 及去，人立石著其功。

translations.literal: When he departed, the people erected a stele recording his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: When he departed, the people erected a stele recording his achievements.

sentences.zh: 後為貴鄉令，有母子相訟者，景駿曰：「令少不天，常自痛。

translations.literal: Later he served as magistrate of Guixiang; when a mother and son sued each other, Jingjun said: 'This magistrate lost his father in youth and always grieves for it.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as magistrate of Guixiang. When a mother and son sued each other, Jingjun said: 'This magistrate lost his father in youth and always grieves for it.

sentences.zh: 爾幸有親，而忘孝邪？

translations.literal: You are fortunate to have a parent — yet you forget filial piety?
translations.idiomatic: You are fortunate to have a parent — yet you forget filial piety?

sentences.zh: 教之不孚，令之罪也。」

translations.literal: If instruction does not win trust, it is the magistrate's fault.'
translations.idiomatic: If instruction does not win trust, it is the magistrate's fault.'

sentences.zh: 因嗚咽流涕，付授《孝經》，使習大義。

translations.literal: He then sobbed with tears flowing, handed them the Classic of Filial Piety, and had them study its great principles.
translations.idiomatic: He then sobbed with tears flowing, handed them the Classic of Filial Piety, and had them study its great principles.

sentences.zh: 於是母子感悟，請自新，遂為孝子。

translations.literal: Thereupon mother and son were moved to understanding, asked to reform themselves, and became filial children.
translations.idiomatic: Mother and son were moved to understanding, asked to reform themselves, and became filial children.

sentences.zh: 當時治有名者：景駿與清漳令馮元淑、臨洺令楊茂謙三人。

translations.literal: At the time those famed for governance were three: Jingjun, Feng Yuanshu magistrate of Qingzhang, and Yang Maoqian magistrate of Linming.
translations.idiomatic: At the time those famed for governance were three: Jingjun, Feng Yuanshu magistrate of Qingzhang, and Yang Maoqian magistrate of Linming.

sentences.zh: 景駿後數年為趙州長史，道出肥鄉，民喜，爭奏酒食迎犒，有小兒亦在中。

translations.literal: Several years later Jingjun served as chief administrator of Zhao Prefecture; passing through Feixiang, the people rejoiced and competed to offer wine and food to welcome and reward him; a small child was also among them.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later Jingjun served as chief administrator of Zhao Prefecture. Passing through Feixiang, the people rejoiced and competed to offer wine and food to welcome him. A small child was also among them.

sentences.zh: 景駿曰：「方兒曹未生，而吾去邑，非有舊恩，何故來？」

translations.literal: Jingjun said: 'When you children were not yet born I had already left the county — there was no old kindness; why have you come?'
translations.idiomatic: Jingjun said: 'When you children were not yet born I had already left the county — there was no old kindness. Why have you come?'

sentences.zh: 對曰：「耆老為我言，學廬、館舍、橋鄣皆公所治，意公為古人，今幸親見，所以來。」

translations.literal: He replied: 'The elders told me that the school halls, guesthouses, bridges, and embankments were all built by you, sir; I thought you were a man of antiquity — now I am fortunate to see you in person, and that is why I came.'
translations.idiomatic: He replied: 'The elders told me that the school halls, guesthouses, bridges, and embankments were all built by you. I thought you were a man of antiquity — now I am fortunate to see you in person, and that is why I came.'

sentences.zh: 景駿為留終日。

translations.literal: Jingjun stayed a full day for their sake.
translations.idiomatic: Jingjun stayed a full day for their sake.

sentences.zh: 後遷房州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to prefect of Fang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was transferred to prefect of Fang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 州窮險，有蠻夷風，無學校，好祀淫鬼，景駿為諸生貢舉，通隘道，作傳舍，罷祠房無名者。

translations.literal: The prefecture was remote and dangerous, with barbarian customs; there were no schools and people favored worship of improper spirits; Jingjun had students recommended for office, opened narrow passes, built relay stations, and abolished shrines to nameless spirits.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture was remote and dangerous, with barbarian customs. There were no schools and people favored worship of improper spirits. Jingjun had students recommended for office, opened narrow passes, built relay stations, and abolished shrines to nameless spirits.

sentences.zh: 景駿之治民，求所以便之，類如此。

translations.literal: In governing the people, Jingjun sought whatever would benefit them — mostly like this.
translations.idiomatic: In governing the people, Jingjun sought whatever would benefit them — mostly like this.

sentences.zh: 轉奉天令，未行，卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to magistrate of Fengtian but died before departing.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to magistrate of Fengtian but died before departing.

sentences.zh: 茂謙擢制舉，授左拾遺內供奉，為吏介而勤，歷秘書郎。

translations.literal: Maoqian passed the policy examination and was appointed left remonstrance official in palace service; as an official he was upright and diligent and served as secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Maoqian passed the policy examination and was appointed left remonstrance official in palace service. As an official he was upright and diligent and served as secretary.

sentences.zh: 始竇懷貞雅重其材，及執政，薦為大理正、左臺御史中丞。

translations.literal: At first Dou Huaizhen greatly valued his talent; when he took power he recommended him as chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review and censor-in-chief of the Left Platform.
translations.idiomatic: At first Dou Huaizhen greatly valued his talent. When he took power he recommended him as chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review and censor-in-chief of the Left Platform.

sentences.zh: 開元初，出為魏州刺史、河北道按察使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan he went out as prefect of Wei Prefecture and inspection commissioner of the Hebei Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Kaiyuan he was posted as prefect of Wei Prefecture and inspection commissioner of the Hebei Circuit.

sentences.zh: 與司馬張懷玉同鄉，長相善，洎晚有隙，掉訐短長，左遷桂州都督。

translations.literal: He was from the same home district as Vice Prefect Zhang Huaiyu; for long they were on good terms, but in later years a rift arose; they slandered each other's faults, and he was demoted to military commissioner of Gui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was from the same home district as Vice Prefect Zhang Huaiyu and for long they were on good terms, but in later years a rift arose. They slandered each other's faults, and he was demoted to military commissioner of Gui Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 徙廣州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Guang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Guang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 景駿子述，自有傳。

translations.literal: Jingjun's son Shu has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Jingjun's son Shu has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 李惠登，營州柳城人，為平盧軍裨將。

translations.literal: Li Huideng was a native of Liucheng in Ying Prefecture and served as deputy general of the Pinglu Army.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huideng was from Liucheng in Ying Prefecture and served as deputy general of the Pinglu Army.

sentences.zh: 安祿山亂，從董秦泛海，略定滄、棣等州。

translations.literal: When the An Lushan rebellion broke out, he followed Dong Qin across the sea and roughly pacified Cang, Di, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When the An Lushan rebellion broke out, he followed Dong Qin across the sea and roughly pacified Cang, Di, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 輕兵遠鬥，賊不支，戰輒北。

translations.literal: With light troops fighting far from base, the rebels could not hold and fled north in every battle.
translations.idiomatic: With light troops fighting far from base, the rebels could not hold and fled north in every battle.

sentences.zh: 史思明反，惠登陷賊，以計挺身走山南，依來瑱，表試金吾衛將軍。

translations.literal: When Shi Siming rebelled, Huideng fell into rebel hands but by stratagem boldly escaped to Shannan, attached himself to Lai Tian, and was provisionally appointed general of the Golden Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Siming rebelled, Huideng fell into rebel hands but by stratagem boldly escaped to Shannan, attached himself to Lai Tian, and was provisionally appointed general of the Golden Guard.

sentences.zh: 李希烈反，屬以兵二千，使屯隋州，惠登挈州以歸，即拜刺史。

translations.literal: When Li Xilie rebelled, he was assigned two thousand troops and ordered to garrison Sui Prefecture; Huideng brought the prefecture back in submission and was immediately appointed prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xilie rebelled, he was assigned two thousand troops and ordered to garrison Sui Prefecture. Huideng brought the prefecture back in submission and was immediately appointed prefect.

sentences.zh: 州數被亂，野如蓺，人無處業。

translations.literal: The prefecture had repeatedly suffered disorder; the fields were like wasteland and people had no place to settle.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture had repeatedly suffered disorder. The fields were like wasteland and people had no place to settle.

sentences.zh: 惠登雖樸素無學術，而視人所謂利者行之，所謂害者去之，率心所安，暗與古合。

translations.literal: Although Huideng was plain and unlearned, he did what people called beneficial and removed what they called harmful; following what his heart found right, he unknowingly accorded with ancient ways.
translations.idiomatic: Although Huideng was plain and unlearned, he did what people called beneficial and removed what they called harmful. Following what his heart found right, he unknowingly accorded with ancient ways.

sentences.zh: 政清靜，居二十年，田畝辟，戶口日增，人歌舞之。

translations.literal: His governance was clear and quiet; he remained twenty years; fields were opened, households daily increased, and people sang songs of praise.
translations.idiomatic: His governance was clear and quiet. He remained twenty years; fields were opened, households daily increased, and people sang songs of praise.

sentences.zh: 於是節度使於頔狀其績，詔加御史大夫，升隋為上州。

translations.literal: Thereupon Military Commissioner Yu Di reported his achievements; an edict added the title of censor grandee and elevated Sui to a upper-grade prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Military Commissioner Yu Di reported his achievements. An edict added the title of censor grandee and elevated Sui to an upper-grade prefecture.

sentences.zh: 俄檢校國子祭酒，卒，贈洪州都督。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed acting director of the Directorate of Education; he died and was posthumously made military commissioner of Hong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed acting director of the Directorate of Education. He died and was posthumously made military commissioner of Hong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 羅向，越州會稽人。

translations.literal: Luo Xiang was a native of Kuaiji in Yue Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Xiang was from Kuaiji in Yue Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 寶應初，詣闕上書，授太常寺太祝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoying he went to the palace gate and submitted a memorial; he was appointed grand invoker of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Baoying he went to the palace gate and submitted a memorial. He was appointed grand invoker of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 曹王臯領江西、荊襄節度使，常署幕府，遷累副使。

translations.literal: Prince of Cao Li Gao held the post of military commissioner of Jiangxi and Jingxiang; Xiang was often assigned to his staff and was repeatedly promoted to vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Cao Li Gao held the post of military commissioner of Jiangxi and Jingxiang. Xiang was often assigned to his staff and rose to vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 臯卒，軍亂，劫府軍，向取首惡十餘人斬以徇，環棘廷中，俾投所劫庫物，一日皆滿，乃貰餘黨。

translations.literal: When Gao died, the army mutinied and plundered the headquarters stores; Xiang took more than ten chief culprits and executed them as a warning, surrounded the thorn hedge in the courtyard, had them throw back what they had plundered from the stores, and in one day all was full; then he pardoned the remaining followers.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao died, the army mutinied and plundered the headquarters stores. Xiang took more than ten chief culprits and executed them as a warning, surrounded the thorn hedge in the courtyard, had them throw back what they had plundered, and in one day all was restored. Then he pardoned the remaining followers.

sentences.zh: 召為奉天令。

translations.literal: He was summoned as magistrate of Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as magistrate of Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 中官出入系道，吏緣以犯禁，向搒笞之，雖死不置，自是屏息。

translations.literal: Eunuchs coming and going thronged the roads; officials used this to violate prohibitions; Xiang beat them with the bastinado and would not stop even if they died; from then on they fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs coming and going thronged the roads, and officials used this to violate prohibitions. Xiang beat them with the bastinado and would not stop even if they died. From then on they fell silent.

sentences.zh: 擢廬州刺史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to prefect of Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to prefect of Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 民間病者，舍醫藥，禱淫祀，向下令止之。

translations.literal: Among the people, the sick abandoned medicine and prayed at improper shrines; Prefect Xiang ordered this stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Among the people, the sick abandoned medicine and prayed at improper shrines. Prefect Xiang ordered this stopped.

sentences.zh: 修學官，政教簡易，有芝草、白雀。

translations.literal: He repaired the school halls; his governance and instruction were simple and easy; there appeared auspicious fungus-grass and white magpies.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired the school halls. His governance and instruction were simple and easy, and auspicious fungus-grass and white magpies appeared.

sentences.zh: 淮南節度使杜佑上治狀，賜金紫服。

translations.literal: Military Commissioner of Huainan Du You submitted a report on his governance and was granted gold and purple robes.
translations.idiomatic: Military Commissioner of Huainan Du You submitted a report on his governance and was granted gold and purple robes.

sentences.zh: 再遷京兆尹，請減平糴半，以常賦充之，人賴其利。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, requested halving the equalizing grain purchase, and used regular tax revenue to cover it; the people relied on this benefit.
translations.idiomatic: He was again transferred to metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, requested halving the equalizing grain purchase, and used regular tax revenue to cover it. The people benefited greatly.

sentences.zh: 以老病求解，徙太子賓客，累封襄陽縣男。

translations.literal: On account of old age and illness he requested release, was transferred to guest of the heir apparent, and was repeatedly enfeoffed as Baron of Xiangyang County.
translations.idiomatic: On account of old age and illness he requested release, was transferred to guest of the heir apparent, and was repeatedly enfeoffed as Baron of Xiangyang County.

sentences.zh: 卒，謚曰夷。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously titled Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously titled Yi.

sentences.zh: 子讓，字景宣，以文學蚤有譽。

translations.literal: His son Rang, styled Jingxuan, was early famed for literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rang, styled Jingxuan, was early famed for literary learning.

sentences.zh: 舉進士、宏辭、賢良方正，皆高第，為咸陽尉。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi, grand rhetoric, and worthy and upright examinations, all with top ranks, and served as aide of Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi, grand rhetoric, and worthy and upright examinations, all with top ranks, and served as aide of Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 父喪，幾毀滅。

translations.literal: When his father died, he nearly wasted away in grief.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, he nearly wasted away in grief.

sentences.zh: 服除，布衣糲飯，不應辟署十餘年。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he wore plain cloth and ate coarse rice and did not respond to appointments for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, he wore plain cloth and ate coarse rice and did not accept appointments for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 淮南節度使李鄘即所居敦請置幕府，除監察御史，位給事中，累遷福建觀察使，兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: Military Commissioner of Huainan Li Yong, at the place where Rang lived, earnestly invited him to join his staff; he was appointed investigating censor, rose to attendant censor, and was repeatedly promoted to observation commissioner of Fujian, concurrently censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Military Commissioner of Huainan Li Yong, at the place where Rang lived, earnestly invited him to join his staff. He was appointed investigating censor, rose to attendant censor, and was promoted to observation commissioner of Fujian, concurrently censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 有仁惠名。

translations.literal: He had a reputation for benevolence and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: He had a reputation for benevolence and kindness.

sentences.zh: 或以婢遺讓者，問所從，答曰：「女兄九人皆為官所賣，留者獨老母耳。」

translations.literal: When someone gave Rang a maidservant, he asked where she came from; the reply was: 'Nine elder sisters were all sold by officials; the one left is only an old mother.'
translations.idiomatic: When someone gave Rang a maidservant, he asked where she came from. The reply was: 'Nine elder sisters were all sold by officials; the one left is only an old mother.'

sentences.zh: 讓慘然，為燹券，召母歸之。

translations.literal: Rang was deeply moved, made a deed of manumission, and summoned the mother to take her back.
translations.idiomatic: Rang was deeply moved, made a deed of manumission, and summoned the mother to take her back.

sentences.zh: 入為散騎常侍，拜江西觀察使。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as attendant cavalryman-at-large and was appointed observation commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as attendant cavalryman-at-large and was appointed observation commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十一，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-one and was posthumously made minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-one and was posthumously made minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 韋丹，字文明，京兆萬年人，周大司空孝寬六世孫。

translations.literal: Wei Dan, styled Wenming, was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao, sixth-generation descendant of Zhou Grand Minister of Works Xiaokuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Dan, styled Wenming, was from Wannian in Jingzhao, sixth-generation descendant of Zhou Grand Minister of Works Xiaokuan.

sentences.zh: 高祖琨，以洗馬事太子承乾，諫不聽。

translations.literal: His ancestor Kun served as palace attendant to Crown Prince Chengqian and remonstrated but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Kun served as palace attendant to Crown Prince Chengqian and remonstrated but was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 太宗才之，擢給事中。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong valued his talent and promoted him to attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong valued his talent and promoted him to attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 高宗在東宮，為中舍人，封武陽縣侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong was in the Eastern Palace, Kun served as middle palace attendant and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuyang County.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong was in the Eastern Palace, Kun served as middle palace attendant and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuyang County.

sentences.zh: 孝敬為太子，琨以右中護為詹事。

translations.literal: When Xiaojing was crown prince, Kun served as right middle guard and grand tutor.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaojing was crown prince, Kun served as right middle guard and grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈秦州都督，謚曰貞。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made military commissioner of Qin Prefecture and titled Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made military commissioner of Qin Prefecture and titled Zhen.

sentences.zh: 丹蚤孤，從外祖顏真卿學，擢明經，調安遠令，以讓庶兄，入紫閣山事從父能。

translations.literal: Dan was orphaned early, studied under his maternal grandfather Yan Zhenqing, passed the illuminated classics examination, was assigned magistrate of Anyuan, yielded the post to his elder half-brother, and entered Mount Zige to serve his father's younger cousin Neng.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was orphaned early and studied under his maternal grandfather Yan Zhenqing. He passed the illuminated classics examination, was assigned magistrate of Anyuan, yielded the post to his elder half-brother, and entered Mount Zige to serve his father's younger cousin Neng.

sentences.zh: 復舉《五經》高第，歷咸陽尉，張獻甫表佐邠寧幕府。

translations.literal: He again placed at the top in the Five Classics examination, served as aide of Xianyang, and was recommended by Zhang Xianfu to join the Binning staff.
translations.idiomatic: He again placed at the top in the Five Classics examination, served as aide of Xianyang, and was recommended by Zhang Xianfu to join the Binning staff.

sentences.zh: 順宗為太子，以殿中侍御史召為舍人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shunzong was crown prince, he was summoned as palace attendant from his post as attendant censor within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shunzong was crown prince, he was summoned as palace attendant from his post as attendant censor within the palace.

sentences.zh: 新羅國君死，詔拜司封郎中往吊。

translations.literal: When the king of Silla died, an edict appointed him director in the Bureau of Enfeoffment to go and offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: When the king of Silla died, an edict appointed him director in the Bureau of Enfeoffment to go and offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 故事，使外國，賜州縣十官，賣以取貲，號「私覿官」。

translations.literal: By precedent, envoys to foreign states were granted ten prefecture and county offices to sell for funds, called 'private audience offices.'
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, envoys to foreign states were granted ten prefecture and county offices to sell for funds, called 'private audience offices.'

sentences.zh: 丹曰：「使外國，不足於資，宜上請，安有貿官受錢？」

translations.literal: Dan said: 'When serving abroad, if funds are insufficient one should petition above — how could one trade offices for money?'
translations.idiomatic: Dan said: 'When serving abroad, if funds are insufficient one should petition above — how could one trade offices for money?'

sentences.zh: 即具疏所宜費，帝命有司與之，因著令。

translations.literal: He immediately submitted a detailed memorial of necessary expenses; the emperor ordered the relevant offices to provide them and thereby established a regulation.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately submitted a detailed memorial of necessary expenses. The emperor ordered the relevant offices to provide them and established a regulation.

sentences.zh: 未行，而新羅立君死，還為容州刺史。

translations.literal: Before departing, the newly enthroned king of Silla died; he returned and was made prefect of Rong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before departing, the newly enthroned king of Silla died. He returned and was made prefect of Rong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 教民耕織，止惰遊，興學校，民貧自鬻者，贖歸之，禁吏不得掠為隸。

translations.literal: He taught the people farming and weaving, stopped idle wandering, established schools, ransomed back those who sold themselves in poverty, and forbade officials from seizing people as slaves.
translations.idiomatic: He taught the people farming and weaving, stopped idle wandering, and established schools. He ransomed back those who sold themselves in poverty and forbade officials from seizing people as slaves.

sentences.zh: 始城州，周十三里，屯田二十四所，教種茶、麥，仁化大行。

translations.literal: He first walled the prefectural seat, thirteen li in circumference, established twenty-four military colonies, taught planting of tea and wheat, and benevolent transformation flourished greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He first walled the prefectural seat, thirteen li in circumference, established twenty-four military colonies, taught planting of tea and wheat, and benevolent transformation flourished greatly.

sentences.zh: 遷河南少尹，未至，徙義成軍司馬。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice governor of Henan but before arriving was moved to vice administrator of the Yicheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice governor of Henan but, before arriving, was moved to vice administrator of the Yicheng Army.

sentences.zh: 以諫議大夫召，有直名。

translations.literal: He was summoned as remonstrance grandee and had a reputation for uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as remonstrance grandee and had a reputation for uprightness.

sentences.zh: 劉辟反，議者欲釋不誅，丹上疏，以為「孝文世，法廢人慢，當濟以威，今不誅辟，則可使者唯兩京耳」。

translations.literal: When Liu Pi rebelled, some in council wished to release him without execution; Dan submitted a memorial, arguing: 'In the time of Emperor Xiaowen of Han, the law was neglected and people were insolent — authority should supplement it. If Pi is not executed now, the only places one can send envoys will be the two capitals alone.'
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Pi rebelled, some in council wished to release him without execution. Dan submitted a memorial arguing: 'In Emperor Xiaowen's time, the law was neglected and people were insolent — authority should supplement it. If Pi is not executed now, envoys can be sent only to the two capitals.'

sentences.zh: 憲宗褒美。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong praised him.

sentences.zh: 會辟圍梓州，乃授丹劍南東川節度使，代李康。

translations.literal: When Pi besieged Zizhou, Dan was appointed military commissioner of Eastern Sichuan in Jiannan to replace Li Kang.
translations.idiomatic: When Pi besieged Zizhou, Dan was appointed military commissioner of Eastern Sichuan in Jiannan to replace Li Kang.

sentences.zh: 至漢中，上言康守方盡力，不可易。

translations.literal: Reaching Hanzhong, he memorialized that Kang was defending with full effort and should not be replaced.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Hanzhong, he memorialized that Kang was defending with full effort and should not be replaced.

sentences.zh: 召還議蜀事。

translations.literal: He was recalled to discuss affairs in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to discuss affairs in Shu.

sentences.zh: 辟去梓，因以讓高崇文，乃拜晉慈隰州觀察使，封咸陽郡公。

translations.literal: When Pi left Zizhou, Dan yielded the post to Gao Chongwen and was appointed observation commissioner of Jin, Ci, and Xi prefectures, enfeoffed as Duke of Xianyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Pi left Zizhou, Dan yielded the post to Gao Chongwen and was appointed observation commissioner of Jin, Ci, and Xi prefectures, enfeoffed as Duke of Xianyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 閱歲，自陳所治三州，非要害地，不足張職，為國家費，不如屬之河東，帝從之。

translations.literal: After a year he stated that the three prefectures he governed were not strategic territory, insufficient to justify his office, and a expense to the state — better to attach them to Hedong; the emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he stated that the three prefectures he governed were not strategic territory, insufficient to justify his office, and an expense to the state — better to attach them to Hedong. The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 徙為江南西道觀察使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to observation commissioner of the Western Jiangnan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to observation commissioner of the Western Jiangnan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 丹計口受俸，委余於官，罷八州冗食者，收其財。

translations.literal: Dan calculated salary by headcount, turned surplus over to the government, abolished superfluous eaters in eight prefectures, and recovered their funds.
translations.idiomatic: Dan calculated salary by headcount, turned surplus over to the government, abolished superfluous eaters in eight prefectures, and recovered their funds.

sentences.zh: 始，民不知為瓦屋，草茨竹椽，久燥則戛而焚。

translations.literal: At first the people did not know tile-roofed houses; thatched grass and bamboo rafters, once long dry, would crack and burn.
translations.idiomatic: At first the people did not know tile-roofed houses. Thatched grass and bamboo rafters, once long dry, would crack and burn.

sentences.zh: 丹召工教為陶，聚材於場，度其費為估，不取贏利。

translations.literal: Dan summoned craftsmen to teach tile-making, gathered materials in a yard, estimated costs as the price, and took no profit.
translations.idiomatic: Dan summoned craftsmen to teach tile-making, gathered materials in a yard, estimated costs as the price, and took no profit.

sentences.zh: 人能為屋者，受材瓦於官，免半賦，徐取其償；

translations.literal: Those who could build houses received timber and tiles from the government, were exempted half their tax levy, and repaid gradually;
translations.idiomatic: Those who could build houses received timber and tiles from the government, were exempted half their tax levy, and repaid gradually;

sentences.zh: 逃未復者，官為為之；

translations.literal: those who had fled and not returned, the government built for them;
translations.idiomatic: those who had fled and not returned, the government built for them;

sentences.zh: 貧不能者，畀以財；

translations.literal: those too poor to manage, funds were given;
translations.idiomatic: those too poor to manage were given funds;

sentences.zh: 身往勸督。

translations.literal: he went in person to encourage and supervise.
translations.idiomatic: he went in person to encourage and supervise.

sentences.zh: 置南北市，為營以舍軍，歲中旱，募人就功，厚與直，給其食。

translations.literal: He established north and south markets and built camps to house troops; midyear drought came and he recruited laborers for public works, paid them generously, and provided food.
translations.idiomatic: He established north and south markets and built camps to house troops. When midyear drought came, he recruited laborers for public works, paid them generously, and provided food.

sentences.zh: 為衢南北夾兩營，東西七里。

translations.literal: He made the thoroughfare with two camps flanking north and south, seven li east to west.
translations.idiomatic: He made the thoroughfare with two camps flanking north and south, seven li east to west.

sentences.zh: 以廢倉為新廄，馬息不死。

translations.literal: He converted abandoned granaries into new stables; horses ceased dying.
translations.idiomatic: He converted abandoned granaries into new stables, and horses ceased dying.

sentences.zh: 築堤捍江，長十二里，竇以疏漲。

translations.literal: He built dikes to hold back the river, twelve li long, with sluices to drain floodwater.
translations.idiomatic: He built dikes twelve li long to hold back the river, with sluices to drain floodwater.

sentences.zh: 凡為陂塘五百九十八所，灌田萬二千頃。

translations.literal: In all he made five hundred ninety-eight reservoirs and ponds, irrigating twelve thousand qing of fields.
translations.idiomatic: In all he made five hundred ninety-eight reservoirs and ponds, irrigating twelve thousand qing of fields.

sentences.zh: 有吏主倉十年，丹覆其糧，亡三千斛，丹曰：「吏豈自費邪？」

translations.literal: An official had managed a granary ten years; Dan audited the grain and found three thousand hu missing; Dan said: 'Would an official consume it himself?'
translations.idiomatic: An official had managed a granary ten years. Dan audited the grain and found three thousand hu missing. Dan said: 'Would an official consume it himself?'

sentences.zh: 籍其家，盡得文記，乃權吏所奪，召諸吏曰：「若恃權取於倉，罪也。

translations.literal: He registered the official's household and found full written records — it was powerful officials who had taken it; he summoned all officials and said: 'If you rely on power to take from the granary, it is a crime.
translations.idiomatic: He registered the official's household and found full written records — powerful officials had taken it. He summoned all officials and said: 'If you rely on power to take from the granary, it is a crime.

sentences.zh: 與若期，一月還之。」

translations.literal: I give you a deadline — return it within one month.'
translations.idiomatic: I give you a deadline — return it within one month.'

sentences.zh: 皆頓首謝，及期無敢違。

translations.literal: All kowtowed in thanks, and when the deadline came none dared violate it.
translations.idiomatic: All kowtowed in thanks, and when the deadline came none dared violate it.

sentences.zh: 有卒違令當死，釋不誅，去，上書告丹不法，詔丹解官待辨。

translations.literal: A soldier violated orders and deserved death; Dan released him without execution; the man left and submitted a memorial accusing Dan of illegal conduct; an edict ordered Dan to resign and await investigation.
translations.idiomatic: A soldier violated orders and deserved death; Dan released him without execution. The man left and submitted a memorial accusing Dan of illegal conduct. An edict ordered Dan to resign and await investigation.

sentences.zh: 會卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: He happened to die at fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He happened to die at fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 驗卒所告，皆不實，丹治狀愈明。

translations.literal: Verification showed the soldier's accusations were all false; Dan's record of governance became even clearer.
translations.idiomatic: Verification showed the soldier's accusations were all false, and Dan's record of governance became even clearer.

sentences.zh: 太和中，裴誼觀察江西，上言為丹立祠堂，刻石紀功，不報。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era, Pei Yi, observing Jiangxi, memorialized to erect a shrine for Dan and inscribe stone recording his achievements; no response was given.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe era, Pei Yi, observing Jiangxi, memorialized to erect a shrine for Dan and inscribe stone recording his achievements. No response was given.

sentences.zh: 宣宗讀《元和實錄》，見丹政事卓然，它日與宰相語：「元和時治民孰第一？」

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong read the Veritable Records of Yuanhe and saw Dan's governance was outstanding; one day he said to the chief ministers: 'In the Yuanhe era who was first in governing the people?'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong read the Veritable Records of Yuanhe and saw Dan's governance was outstanding. One day he said to the chief ministers: 'In the Yuanhe era who was first in governing the people?'

sentences.zh: 周墀對：「臣嘗守江西，韋丹有大功，德被八州，歿四十年，老幼思之不忘。」

translations.literal: Zhou Chi replied: 'Your servant once governed Jiangxi; Wei Dan had great achievements, his virtue covered eight prefectures, and though dead forty years, old and young still remember him without forgetting.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Chi replied: 'I once governed Jiangxi. Wei Dan had great achievements, his virtue covered eight prefectures, and though dead forty years, old and young still remember him.'

sentences.zh: 乃詔觀察使紇幹上丹功狀，命刻功於碑。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered Observation Commissioner Qian Gan to submit Dan's record of achievements and commanded his merits be carved on a stele.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered Observation Commissioner Qian Gan to submit Dan's record of achievements and commanded his merits be carved on a stele.

sentences.zh: 子宙，推蔭累調河南府司錄參軍，李玨表河陽幕府。

translations.literal: His son Zhou, through inherited privilege, was repeatedly assigned recorder of Henan Prefecture; Li Jue recommended him to the Heyang staff.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhou, through inherited privilege, was repeatedly assigned recorder of Henan Prefecture. Li Jue recommended him to the Heyang staff.

sentences.zh: 宣宗謂宰相墀曰：「丹有子否？」

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong said to Chief Minister Chi: 'Does Dan have a son?'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong said to Chief Minister Chi: 'Does Dan have a son?'

sentences.zh: 以宙對。

translations.literal: He answered with Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: He answered with Zhou.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「與好官。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'Give him a good office.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: 'Give him a good office.'

sentences.zh: 乃拜侍御史，三遷度支郎中。

translations.literal: He was then appointed attendant censor and was thrice promoted to director in the Bureau of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed attendant censor and rose to director in the Bureau of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 盧鈞節度太原，表宙為副。

translations.literal: Lu Jun commanded Taiyuan and recommended Zhou as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jun commanded Taiyuan and recommended Zhou as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 是時，回鶻已破諸部，入塞下，剽殺吏民。

translations.literal: At this time the Uyghurs had broken various tribes and entered within the passes, plundering and killing officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the Uyghurs had broken various tribes and entered within the passes, plundering and killing officials and people.

sentences.zh: 鈞欲得信重吏視邊，宙請往。

translations.literal: Jun wished to send a trusted and weighty official to inspect the frontier; Zhou requested to go.
translations.idiomatic: Jun wished to send a trusted official to inspect the frontier; Zhou requested to go.

sentences.zh: 自定襄、雁門、五原，絕武州塞，略雲中，逾句註，遍見酋豪，鐫諭之；

translations.literal: From Dingxiang, Yanmen, and Wuyuan, crossing Wuzhou Pass, traversing Yunzhong, passing Juzhu, he met chieftains everywhere and engraved proclamations to instruct them;
translations.idiomatic: From Dingxiang, Yanmen, and Wuyuan, crossing Wuzhou Pass, traversing Yunzhong, and passing Juzhu, he met chieftains everywhere and engraved proclamations to instruct them;

sentences.zh: 視亭障守卒，增其稟；

translations.literal: he inspected frontier posts and garrison soldiers and increased their rations;
translations.idiomatic: he inspected frontier posts and garrison soldiers and increased their rations;

sentences.zh: 約吏不得擅以兵侵諸戎，犯者死，於是三部六蕃諸種皆信悅。

translations.literal: he stipulated that officials must not on their own authority use troops to invade the various barbarians — violators would die; thereupon the three departments, six tribes, and various peoples all trusted and were pleased.
translations.idiomatic: he stipulated that officials must not on their own authority use troops to invade the various barbarians — violators would die. Thereupon the three departments, six tribes, and various peoples all trusted and were pleased.

sentences.zh: 召拜吏部郎中。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 出為永州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 州方災歉，乃斥官下什用所以供刺史者，得九十餘萬錢，為市糧餉。

translations.literal: The prefecture was suffering disaster and famine; he sold off the various goods under official use that supplied the prefect and obtained more than nine hundred thousand cash to buy grain provisions.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture was suffering disaster and famine. He sold off the various goods under official use that supplied the prefect and obtained more than nine hundred thousand cash to buy grain provisions.

sentences.zh: 俗不知法，多觸罪，宙為書制律，並種植為生之宜，戶給之。

translations.literal: Custom did not know law and many violated it; Zhou wrote out regulations and laws, together with what was suitable for planting and livelihood, and gave them to each household.
translations.idiomatic: The people did not know the law and many violated it. Zhou wrote out regulations and laws, together with what was suitable for planting and livelihood, and gave them to each household.

sentences.zh: 州負嶺，轉餉艱險，每饑，人輒莩死，宙始築常平倉，收谷羨余以待乏。

translations.literal: The prefecture backed on mountains; transporting provisions was difficult and dangerous; each famine people died of starvation on the roads; Zhou first built ever-normal granaries, collected surplus grain to await shortage.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture backed on mountains and transporting provisions was difficult and dangerous. Each famine people died of starvation on the roads. Zhou first built ever-normal granaries and collected surplus grain to await shortage.

sentences.zh: 罷冗役九百四十四員。

translations.literal: He abolished nine hundred forty-four superfluous corvée laborers.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished nine hundred forty-four superfluous corvée laborers.

sentences.zh: 縣舊置吏督賦，宙俾民自輸，家十相保，常先期。

translations.literal: Counties formerly set officials to supervise tax collection; Zhou had the people deliver taxes themselves, with ten households mutually guaranteeing one another, and they regularly paid ahead of schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Counties formerly set officials to supervise tax collection. Zhou had the people deliver taxes themselves, with ten households mutually guaranteeing one another, and they regularly paid ahead of schedule.

sentences.zh: 湘源生零陵香，歲市上供，人苦之，宙為奏罷。

translations.literal: Xiangyuan produced lingling incense; each year it was purchased for imperial tribute and the people suffered; Zhou memorialized to abolish this.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangyuan produced lingling incense purchased each year for imperial tribute, and the people suffered. Zhou memorialized to abolish this.

sentences.zh: 民貧無牛，以力耕，宙為置社，二十家月會錢若干，探名得者先市牛，以是為準，久之，牛不乏。

translations.literal: The people were poor and without oxen, plowing by human strength; Zhou established associations — twenty households monthly pooled a set sum, and by drawing names the winner bought an ox first; using this standard, over time oxen were never lacking.
translations.idiomatic: The people were poor and without oxen, plowing by human strength. Zhou established associations — twenty households monthly pooled a set sum, and by drawing names the winner bought an ox first. Over time oxen were never lacking.

sentences.zh: 立學官，取仕家子弟十五人充之。

translations.literal: He established school officials and selected fifteen sons of official families to fill the posts.
translations.idiomatic: He established school officials and selected fifteen sons of official families to fill the posts.

sentences.zh: 初，俚民婚，出財會賓客，號「破酒」，晝夜集，多至數百人，貧者猶數十；

translations.literal: At first when Li people married, they spent wealth gathering guests, called 'breaking wine,' assembling day and night, often reaching several hundred people, the poor still several dozen;
translations.idiomatic: At first when Li people married, they spent wealth gathering guests in feasts called 'breaking wine,' assembling day and night, often reaching several hundred people, the poor still several dozen;

sentences.zh: 力不足，則不迎，至淫奔者。

translations.literal: when strength was insufficient they did not receive the bride, leading even to illicit unions.
translations.idiomatic: when means were insufficient they did not receive the bride, leading even to illicit unions.

sentences.zh: 宙條約，使略如禮，俗遂改。

translations.literal: Zhou set regulations approximating proper ritual, and custom was thereby reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou set regulations approximating proper ritual, and custom was thereby reformed.

sentences.zh: 邑中少年，常以七月擊鼓，群入民家，號「行盜」，皆迎為辨具，謂之「起盆」，後為解素，喧呼{疒只}鬥。

translations.literal: Youths in the district often in the seventh month beat drums, entered households in groups, called it 'going thieving,' and all were welcomed and provided feast goods, termed 'raising the basin'; afterward they undressed and shouted in noisy brawling.
translations.idiomatic: Youths in the district often in the seventh month beat drums, entered households in groups in a custom called 'going thieving,' and all were welcomed and provided feast goods, termed 'raising the basin'; afterward they undressed and shouted in noisy brawling.

sentences.zh: 宙至，一切禁之。

translations.literal: When Zhou arrived, he forbade all of this.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou arrived, he forbade all of this.

sentences.zh: 還為大理少卿。

translations.literal: He returned as vice director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as vice director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 久之，拜江西觀察使，政簡易，南方以為世官。

translations.literal: After a long time he was appointed observation commissioner of Jiangxi; his governance was simple and easy, and the south regarded it as an hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he was appointed observation commissioner of Jiangxi. His governance was simple and easy, and the south regarded it as an hereditary office.

sentences.zh: 遷嶺南節度使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to military commissioner of Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to military commissioner of Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 南詔陷交趾，撫兵積備，以幹聞。

translations.literal: When Nanzhao captured Jiaozhi, he soothed troops and accumulated supplies, and his capability became known.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanzhao captured Jiaozhi, he soothed troops and accumulated supplies, and his capability became known.

sentences.zh: 加檢校尚書左僕射、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: He was additionally appointed acting left vice director of the Department of State Affairs and associate director of the Chancellery and Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally appointed acting left vice director of the Department of State Affairs and associate director of the Chancellery and Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 咸通中卒。

translations.literal: He died in the Xiantong era.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the Xiantong era.

sentences.zh: 宙弟岫，字伯起，亦有名。

translations.literal: Zhou's younger brother Xiu, styled Boqi, was also renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's younger brother Xiu, styled Boqi, was also renowned.

sentences.zh: 宙在嶺南，以從女妻小校劉謙，或諫止之，岫曰：「吾子孫或當依之。」

translations.literal: When Zhou was in Lingnan, he gave a clanswoman in marriage to junior officer Liu Qian; some advised against it; Xiu said: 'Our descendants may someday rely on him.'
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou was in Lingnan, he gave a clanswoman in marriage to junior officer Liu Qian. Some advised against it, but Xiu said: 'Our descendants may someday rely on him.'

sentences.zh: 謙後以功為封州刺史，生二子，即隱、龔。

translations.literal: Later Qian, through merit, became prefect of Feng Prefecture and had two sons — Yin and Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qian, through merit, became prefect of Feng Prefecture and had two sons — Yin and Gong.

sentences.zh: 盧攜舉進士，陋甚，岫獨謂攜必大用。

translations.literal: Lu Xie passed the jinshi examination and was very unimpressive; Xiu alone said Xie would certainly be greatly employed.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xie passed the jinshi examination and was very unimpressive, but Xiu alone said Xie would certainly rise to great employment.

sentences.zh: 攜執政，岫自泗州刺史擢福建觀察使雲。

translations.literal: When Xie took power, Xiu was promoted from prefect of Si Prefecture to observation commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie took power, Xiu was promoted from prefect of Si Prefecture to observation commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 盧弘宣，字子章。

translations.literal: Lu Hongxuan, styled Zizhang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Hongxuan, styled Zizhang.

sentences.zh: 元和中，擢進士第。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanhe era he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 鄭權帥襄陽，辟署幕府。

translations.literal: Zheng Quan commanded Xiangyang and recruited him to his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Quan commanded Xiangyang and recruited him to his staff.

sentences.zh: 李代權，又二人交憾。

translations.literal: Li replaced Quan, and the two men bore mutual resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Li replaced Quan, and the two men bore mutual resentment.

sentences.zh: 弘宣始謁，敕左右謹衛，既與語，見其沖遠，不覺洗然。

translations.literal: When Hongxuan first paid his respects, Li ordered his attendants to guard carefully; once they spoke, he saw Hongxuan's serene distance and felt himself refreshed without knowing it.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongxuan first paid his respects, Li ordered his attendants to guard carefully. Once they spoke, he saw Hongxuan's serene distance and felt himself refreshed.

sentences.zh: 裴度留守東都，表為判官，遷累給事中。

translations.literal: Pei Du remained to guard the eastern capital and recommended him as administrative aide; he was repeatedly promoted to attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du remained to guard the eastern capital and recommended him as administrative aide. He rose to attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 駙馬都尉韋處仁拜虢州刺史，弘宣謂非所任，還詔不下。

translations.literal: Commandant-escort Wei Churen was appointed prefect of Guo Prefecture; Hongxuan said the post was unsuitable for him, and the returning edict was not issued.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant-escort Wei Churen was appointed prefect of Guo Prefecture. Hongxuan said the post was unsuitable for him, and the returning edict was not issued.

sentences.zh: 開成中，山南、江西大水，詔弘宣與吏部郎中崔晉分道賑恤，使有指。

translations.literal: In the Kaicheng era great floods struck Shannan and Jiangxi; an edict ordered Hongxuan and Director in the Ministry of Personnel Cui Jin to divide routes for relief and comfort, giving the mission clear direction.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaicheng era great floods struck Shannan and Jiangxi. An edict ordered Hongxuan and Director in the Ministry of Personnel Cui Jin to divide routes for relief and comfort.

sentences.zh: 還，遷京兆尹、刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: On return he was transferred to metropolitan governor of Jingzhao and vice minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: On return he was transferred to metropolitan governor of Jingzhao and vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 拜劍南東川節度使。

translations.literal: He was appointed military commissioner of Eastern Sichuan in Jiannan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed military commissioner of Eastern Sichuan in Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 時歲饑，盜贅結，酋豪自王，偽署官吏，發敖廥招亡命，聯蓬、瀘、嘉、榮諸州，訹蠻落搖亂，根株磐熾。

translations.literal: At the time famine struck; bandits multiplied and joined together; chieftains proclaimed themselves kings; they falsely appointed officials, opened granaries to recruit fugitives, linked Peng, Lu, Jia, and Rong prefectures, slandered and stirred barbarian settlements, and their roots ran deep and fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Famine struck; bandits multiplied and joined together. Chieftains proclaimed themselves kings, falsely appointed officials, opened granaries to recruit fugitives, and linked Peng, Lu, Jia, and Rong prefectures. They slandered and stirred barbarian settlements, and their roots ran deep and fierce.

sentences.zh: 弘宣下檄脅諭，賊黨稍降，其黠強者署軍中，孱無能還之農。

translations.literal: Hongxuan issued proclamations threatening and instructing; bandit factions gradually submitted; the cunning and strong he enrolled in the army, the weak and incapable he returned to farming.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxuan issued proclamations threatening and instructing. Bandit factions gradually submitted. The cunning and strong he enrolled in the army; the weak and incapable he returned to farming.

sentences.zh: 魁長逃入峽中，吏捕誅之。

translations.literal: The chief leaders fled into the gorges; officials captured and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: The chief leaders fled into the gorges; officials captured and executed them.

sentences.zh: 徙義武節度使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to military commissioner of Yiwu.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to military commissioner of Yiwu.

sentences.zh: 弘宣性寬厚，政目簡省，人便安之，然犯者不甚貸。

translations.literal: Hongxuan's nature was generous and mild; his governing aims were simple and sparing; people found ease in him, yet offenders were not greatly pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxuan was generous and mild; his governing aims were simple and sparing. People found ease in him, yet offenders were not greatly pardoned.

sentences.zh: 河朔故法，偶語軍中則死，弘宣始除之。

translations.literal: By old law north of the Yellow River, casual speech in the army meant death; Hongxuan first abolished this.
translations.idiomatic: By old law north of the Yellow River, casual speech in the army meant death. Hongxuan first abolished this.

sentences.zh: 初，詔賜其軍粟三十萬斛，貯飛狐，弘宣計免費不能滿直，敕吏守之。

translations.literal: At first an edict granted his army three hundred thousand hu of grain stored at Feihu; Hongxuan calculated that transport costs could not cover the value and ordered officials to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: At first an edict granted his army three hundred thousand hu of grain stored at Feihu. Hongxuan calculated that transport costs could not cover the value and ordered officials to guard it.

sentences.zh: 明年春，大旱，教民隨力往取，時幽、魏饑甚，獨易、定自如。

translations.literal: The next spring, great drought came; he instructed the people to go take grain according to their strength; at the time You and Wei were severely famine-stricken, but Yi and Ding alone remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring, great drought came. He instructed the people to take grain according to their strength. You and Wei were severely famine-stricken, but Yi and Ding alone remained as before.

sentences.zh: 至秋，悉收所貸，軍食以饒。

translations.literal: By autumn all loans were collected and army provisions were abundant.
translations.idiomatic: By autumn all loans were collected and army provisions were abundant.

sentences.zh: 歷工部尚書、秘書監，以太子少傅致仕。

translations.literal: He served as minister of public works and director of the Secretariat and retired as vice tutor of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He served as minister of public works and director of the Secretariat and retired as vice tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十七，贈尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-seven and was posthumously made right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-seven and was posthumously made right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 弘宣患士庶人家祭無定儀，乃合十二家法，損益其當，次以為書。

translations.literal: Hongxuan was troubled that gentry and commoners had no fixed ritual for household sacrifice; he combined twelve family methods, adjusted what was appropriate, and arranged them into a book.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxuan was troubled that gentry and commoners had no fixed ritual for household sacrifice. He combined twelve family methods, adjusted what was appropriate, and arranged them into a book.

sentences.zh: 子告，字子有，及進士第，終給事中。

translations.literal: His son Gao, styled Ziyou, passed the jinshi examination and ended as attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gao, styled Ziyou, passed the jinshi examination and ended as attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 薛元賞，亡裏系所來。

translations.literal: Xue Yuanshang — his native place and origin are unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Yuanshang — his native place and origin are unknown.

sentences.zh: 太和初，自司農少卿，出為漢州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe, from vice director of the Ministry of Revenue he went out as prefect of Han Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Taihe, from vice director of the Ministry of Revenue he was posted as prefect of Han Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時李德裕為劍南西川節度使，會維州降，德裕受之以聞，牛僧孺沮其議，執還之。

translations.literal: At the time Li Deyu was military commissioner of Western Sichuan in Jiannan; when Weizhou submitted, Deyu accepted it and reported; Niu Sengru obstructed the proposal and had it returned.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Li Deyu was military commissioner of Western Sichuan in Jiannan. When Weizhou submitted, Deyu accepted it and reported. Niu Sengru obstructed the proposal and had it returned.

sentences.zh: 元賞上書極言可因撫之，潰虜膺腹，不可失。

translations.literal: Yuanshang submitted a memorial strongly arguing that it could be used to soothe them, splitting the enemy's chest and belly — it must not be lost.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshang submitted a memorial strongly arguing that it could be used to soothe them and split the enemy's chest and belly — it must not be lost.

sentences.zh: 不省。

translations.literal: No attention was given.
translations.idiomatic: No attention was given.

sentences.zh: 段文昌代德裕，狀元賞治當最。

translations.literal: Duan Wenchang replaced Deyu and reported Yuanshang's governance as foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Wenchang replaced Deyu and reported Yuanshang's governance as foremost.

sentences.zh: 遷累司農卿、京兆尹。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to minister of revenue and metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to minister of revenue and metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 出為武寧節度使，罷泗口猥稅，人以為便。

translations.literal: He went out as military commissioner of Wuning, abolished the miscellaneous tax at Sikou, and people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as military commissioner of Wuning, abolished the miscellaneous tax at Sikou, and people found it convenient.

sentences.zh: 俄徙邠寧。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Binning.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Binning.

sentences.zh: 會昌中，德裕當國，復拜京兆尹。

translations.literal: In the Huichang era Deyu held power and Yuanshang was again appointed metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the Huichang era Deyu held power and Yuanshang was again appointed metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 都市多俠少年，以黛墨镵膚，誇詭力，剽奪坊閭。

translations.literal: The capital had many swaggering youths who carved their skin with lampblack ink, boasted of strange strength, and plundered wards and lanes.
translations.idiomatic: The capital had many swaggering youths who carved their skin with lampblack ink, boasted of strange strength, and plundered wards and lanes.

sentences.zh: 元賞到府三日，收惡少，杖死三十餘輩，陳諸市，餘黨懼，爭以火滅其文。

translations.literal: Three days after Yuanshang reached his post, he seized wicked youths and beat more than thirty to death, displayed them in the market; the remaining followers feared and competed to burn away their markings with fire.
translations.idiomatic: Three days after Yuanshang reached his post, he seized wicked youths and beat more than thirty to death, displaying them in the market. The remaining followers feared and competed to burn away their markings with fire.

sentences.zh: 元賞長吏事，能推言時弊，件白之。

translations.literal: Yuanshang was skilled in administrative affairs and could analyze and report contemporary abuses, itemizing each one.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshang was skilled in administrative affairs and could analyze and report contemporary abuses, itemizing each one.

sentences.zh: 禁屯怙勢擾府縣，元賞數與爭，不少縱，由是軍暴折戢，百姓賴安。

translations.literal: Forbidden garrisons relied on power to harass prefectures and counties; Yuanshang repeatedly contended with them and did not yield; thereby military violence was curbed and the people relied on peace.
translations.idiomatic: Forbidden garrisons relied on power to harass prefectures and counties. Yuanshang repeatedly contended with them and did not yield. Military violence was thereby curbed and the people relied on peace.

sentences.zh: 就加檢校吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was additionally appointed acting minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally appointed acting minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 閱歲，進工部尚書，領諸道鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: After a year he was promoted to minister of public works and directed the salt and iron transport commissioner of all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he was promoted to minister of public works and directed the salt and iron transport commissioner of all circuits.

sentences.zh: 德裕用元賞弟元龜為京兆少尹，知府事。

translations.literal: Deyu employed Yuanshang's younger brother Yuan Gui as vice governor of Jingzhao to manage prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu employed Yuanshang's younger brother Yuan Gui as vice governor of Jingzhao to manage prefectural affairs.

sentences.zh: 宣宗立，罷德裕，而元龜坐貶崖州司戶參軍，元賞下除袁王傅。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong ascended, Deyu was removed; Yuan Gui was demoted to registrar of Yazhou; Yuanshang was demoted to tutor of Prince Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong ascended, Deyu was removed. Yuan Gui was demoted to registrar of Yazhou and Yuanshang was demoted to tutor of Prince Yuan.

sentences.zh: 久之，復拜昭義節度使，卒。

translations.literal: After a long time he was again appointed military commissioner of Zhaoyi and died.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he was again appointed military commissioner of Zhaoyi and died.

sentences.zh: 何易於，不詳何所人及所以進。

translations.literal: He Yiyu — it is not clear where he was from or how he advanced.
translations.idiomatic: He Yiyu — it is not clear where he was from or how he advanced.

sentences.zh: 為益昌令。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Yichang.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Yichang.

sentences.zh: 縣距州四十里，刺史崔樸常乘春與賓屬泛舟出益昌旁，索民挽繂，易於身引舟，樸驚問狀，易於曰：「方春，百姓耕且蠶，惟令不事，可任其勞。」

translations.literal: The county was forty li from the prefectural seat; Prefect Cui Pu often in spring went boating with guests beside Yichang and demanded the people tow the ropes; Yiyu personally pulled the boat; Pu was startled and asked the reason; Yiyu said: 'It is spring — the people are plowing and raising silkworms; only the magistrate has no tasks and may bear this labor.'
translations.idiomatic: The county was forty li from the prefectural seat. Prefect Cui Pu often in spring went boating with guests beside Yichang and demanded the people tow the ropes. Yiyu personally pulled the boat. Pu was startled and asked why. Yiyu said: 'It is spring — the people are plowing and raising silkworms. Only the magistrate has no tasks and may bear this labor.'

sentences.zh: 樸愧，與賓客疾驅去。

translations.literal: Pu was ashamed and hurried away with his guests.
translations.idiomatic: Pu was ashamed and hurried away with his guests.

sentences.zh: 鹽鐵官榷取茶利，詔下，所在毋敢隱。

translations.literal: Salt and iron officials monopolized tea profits; when the edict was issued, nowhere dared conceal it.
translations.idiomatic: Salt and iron officials monopolized tea profits. When the edict was issued, nowhere dared conceal it.

sentences.zh: 易於視詔書曰：「益昌人不征茶且不可活，矧厚賦毒之乎？」

translations.literal: Yiyu looked at the edict and said: 'The people of Yichang cannot live even without taxing tea — how much less with heavy levies poisoning them?'
translations.idiomatic: Yiyu looked at the edict and said: 'The people of Yichang cannot live even without taxing tea — how much less with heavy levies poisoning them?'

sentences.zh: 命吏閣詔，吏曰：「天子詔何敢拒？

translations.literal: He ordered an official to shelve the edict; the official said: 'How dare one refuse the Son of Heaven's edict?
translations.idiomatic: He ordered an official to shelve the edict. The official said: 'How dare one refuse the emperor's edict?

sentences.zh: 吏坐死，公得免竄邪？」

translations.literal: The official sits condemned to death — can you, sir, escape exile?'
translations.idiomatic: The official sits condemned to death — can you escape exile?'

sentences.zh: 對曰：「吾敢愛一身，移暴於民乎？

translations.literal: He replied: 'How would I dare cherish my own person and shift violence onto the people?
translations.idiomatic: He replied: 'How would I dare cherish my own person and shift violence onto the people?

sentences.zh: 亦不使罪爾曹。」

translations.literal: Nor would I let you all be punished.'
translations.idiomatic: Nor would I let you all be punished.'

sentences.zh: 即自焚之。

translations.literal: He immediately burned it himself.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately burned it himself.

sentences.zh: 觀察使素賢之，不劾也。

translations.literal: The observation commissioner had long valued him and did not impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: The observation commissioner had long valued him and did not impeach him.

sentences.zh: 民有死喪不能具葬者，以俸敕吏為辦。

translations.literal: When people had deaths in the family and could not afford burial, he used his salary and ordered officials to arrange it.
translations.idiomatic: When people had deaths in the family and could not afford burial, he used his salary and ordered officials to arrange it.

sentences.zh: 召高年坐，以問政得失。

translations.literal: He summoned the elderly to sit and asked about the gains and losses of governance.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the elderly to sit and asked about the gains and losses of governance.

sentences.zh: 凡鬥民在廷，易於丁寧指曉枉直，杖楚遣之，不以付吏，獄三年無囚。

translations.literal: Whenever disputing commoners appeared in court, Yiyu earnestly explained right and wrong, beat them with the rod and sent them away, never handing them to officials; for three years the prison had no inmates.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever disputing commoners appeared in court, Yiyu earnestly explained right and wrong, beat them with the rod and sent them away, never handing them to officials. For three years the prison had no inmates.

sentences.zh: 督賦役不忍迫下戶，或以俸代輸。

translations.literal: In supervising tax and corvée levies he could not bear to press lower households and sometimes paid on their behalf from his salary.
translations.idiomatic: In supervising tax and corvée levies he could not bear to press lower households and sometimes paid on their behalf from his salary.

sentences.zh: 饋給往來，傳符外一無所進，故無異稱。

translations.literal: For provisions to travelers, beyond relay warrants he presented nothing else; therefore he had no special reputation.
translations.idiomatic: For provisions to travelers, beyond relay warrants he presented nothing else; therefore he had no special reputation.

sentences.zh: 以中上考，遷羅江令。

translations.literal: With an upper-middle evaluation he was transferred to magistrate of Luojiang.
translations.idiomatic: With an upper-middle evaluation he was transferred to magistrate of Luojiang.

sentences.zh: 刺史裴休嘗至其邑，導侍不過三人，廉約蓋資性雲。

translations.literal: Prefect Pei Xiu once came to his district; escorts and attendants numbered no more than three — frugality and restraint were likely his nature.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Pei Xiu once came to his district; escorts and attendants numbered no more than three — frugality and restraint were likely his nature.
